title: Reports
purpose: Lets HR/management read a month's attendance totals per employee and every employee's leave used-vs-accrued balances, and download the raw attendance CSV for that month.
layout: Rendered inside the AppShell chrome (app/admin/layout.jsx wraps everything in <AppShell>). SHELL: body background is slate-100; a fixed left sidebar (~white, w-64, logo at top, scrollable nav, collapsible on mobile behind a hamburger) and a top bar with the company name / notification bell / user menu; the page content sits in the main area with normal page padding. Sidebar nav under a 'Management' section heading, in this order: Overview (/admin), Employees, Attendance, Leave Management, Leave Balances, Documents, Reports (ACTIVE here), Analytics, Settings, Email Log, Roles & Access; below that a standalone 'Change Password' item. PAGE BODY, top to bottom, single full-width column: (1) PageHeader — flex row, flex-wrap, items-center, justify-between, gap-3, mb-6. Left: h1 'Reports' (text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800) with p subtitle 'Attendance and leave utilization summaries' (text-sm text-slate-500 mt-0.5). Right: a flex items-center gap-2 group holding the MonthPicker then the Export button. (2) Optional error Alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (3) Card 1 'Monthly Attendance Summary' — class `card overflow-x-auto mb-8` (white, rounded-xl, border-slate-200, shadow-sm), heading in a px-4 pt-4 div, table below with mt-3, table is min-w-full with divide-y divide-slate-200. (4) Card 2 'Leave Utilization' — same card treatment, no bottom margin. No sidebars, no tabs, no right rail. Both tables scroll horizontally inside their own card (overflow-x-auto), not the page. Brand color is blue: brand-600 #1d4ed8, brand-700 #1e40af, brand-500 #2563eb, brand-50 #f0f6ff.

widgets.label: Month navigator (MonthPicker) — sits in the PageHeader right slot
widgets.detail: Three parts in a flex items-center gap-2 row: [←] a btn-secondary button (white bg, border-slate-300, text-slate-700, rounded-lg, hover:bg-slate-50, px forced to 0.75rem via !px-3) whose label is the literal left-arrow glyph '←'; a center <span> with min-width 150px and text-center holding the month label as a block, text-sm font-semibold text-slate-700, formatted 'September 2026' (full month name + 4-digit year, en-US); [→] an identical btn-secondary with the right-arrow glyph '→'. NOTE: this instance is rendered WITHOUT a periodLabel prop, so the optional second sub-line (the 11px slate-400 payroll-cycle date range, e.g. '25 Aug – 24 Sep 2026') is NOT shown on this page even though the component supports it. Clicking ← at January rolls back to December of the previous year; clicking → at December rolls forward to January of the next year. Changing the month refetches ONLY the attendance table.

widgets.label: Export Attendance CSV
widgets.detail: A single btn-secondary button: white background, 1px slate-300 border, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium, text-slate-700, hover:bg-slate-50, inline-flex items-center gap-2. Contains a 16px lucide 'Download' icon at the left, then the text 'Export Attendance CSV'. No dropdown, no options — one click downloads the file for the currently selected month as attendance-2026-09.csv. The downloaded CSV's columns are, in order: Employee Code, Name, Date, Status, Entry Time, Exit Time, Late Mark.

widgets.label: Error banner (conditional)
widgets.detail: Only rendered when a fetch fails; sits between the PageHeader and the first card in a `mb-4` wrapper. Styling: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50, text-red-700, border-red-200. Full page width. Shows the raw backend error message text. It does NOT replace the page — both cards still render below it. Unlike Analytics, this page degrades gracefully.

widgets.label: Monthly Attendance Summary (Card 1)
widgets.detail: Card heading above the table: h3 'Monthly Attendance Summary', font-bold text-slate-800, in a px-4 pt-4 div. Table: min-w-full, divide-y divide-slate-200, mt-3; thead has bg-slate-50; tbody rows divide-y divide-slate-100 with hover:bg-slate-50. Header cells use class `th` = px-4 py-3, text-left, text-xs, font-semibold, text-slate-500, uppercase, tracking-wider. Body cells use class `td` = px-4 py-3, text-sm. EXACT COLUMN HEADERS IN ORDER (9 columns): 'Code' | 'Name' | 'Department' | 'Present' | 'WFH' | 'Half Days' | 'Absent' | 'Leave' | 'Late Marks'. Per-cell rendering: Code = employee code, font-semibold; Name = plain; Department = plain, renders an em-dash '—' when the employee has no department; Present = text-emerald-700 font-medium; WFH = plain; Half Days = plain; Absent = text-red-600 font-medium; Leave = text-purple-700; Late Marks = plain. Every numeric cell falls back to the literal 0 when null. Rows are ordered by employee code ascending, and only Active employees appear. The counts cover the PAYROLL CYCLE for the selected month (e.g. 25 Aug – 24 Sep for 'September'), not the calendar month. This table has NO empty-state row — if there are no employees the tbody is simply blank.

widgets.label: Leave Utilization (Card 2)
widgets.detail: Card heading: h3 'Leave Utilization — used / accrued (balance)', font-bold text-slate-800, in a px-4 pt-4 div (note the em-dash and the lowercase parenthetical — reproduce exactly). Same table/th/td styling as Card 1. COLUMNS ARE DYNAMIC: two fixed leading columns 'Code' and 'Name', then ONE COLUMN PER LEAVE-TYPE CODE found in the data, in first-seen order. The seeded/default codes for a tenant are CL, EL, SL, CO and UL — so the realistic header row is: 'Code' | 'Name' | 'CL' | 'EL' | 'SL' | 'CO' | 'UL' (7 columns). Headers show the short CODE only, never the full leave-type name. Each leave cell renders a small two-line stack: line 1 is `<used>` in font-medium followed by ' / ' and then `<accrued>` in normal weight; line 2 is a block, 11px font-size, text-brand-700 (#1e40af), reading 'bal <balance>' (lowercase 'bal', then the number). Accrued and balance are numbers rounded to 2 dp with trailing zeros dropped (6, 9, 4.5, 3.75 — never '6.00'). A cell for a leave type the employee has no balance row for renders a bare em-dash '—'. Row order is by employee code ascending; Active employees only. IMPORTANT: this table is loaded ONCE on mount and is NOT affected by the month navigator — changing the month leaves it untouched.

widgets.label: Empty state row — Leave Utilization only
widgets.detail: When there are zero rows, the tbody renders a single <tr> with one <td> spanning (2 + number of leave-type columns) columns — i.e. colSpan=7 with the default five leave types — containing the centered text 'No employees yet.' in text-slate-500 with py-8 vertical padding.

widgets.label: Loading spinner (per card)
widgets.detail: Each card independently swaps its table for a Spinner while its data is null: a centered flex container with py-16 vertical padding holding an 8x8 (2rem) circle, border-4, border-slate-200 with border-t-brand-600, animate-spin. Card 1 shows this on first load AND again every time the month is changed (the attendance state is reset to null before each refetch). Card 2 shows it only on first load. The card shell, border and heading stay visible behind the spinner.

actions: Click ← in the month navigator: step back one month (rolls to December of the previous year from January); clears the attendance table to a spinner and refetches the Monthly Attendance Summary for the new month. Leave Utilization is untouched.
Click → in the month navigator: step forward one month (rolls to January of the next year from December); same refetch behaviour.

Click 'Export Attendance CSV': downloads the per-day attendance CSV for the currently selected month as attendance-2026-09.csv (filename pattern attendance-YYYY-MM.csv). The file is fetched as an authenticated blob and saved via a synthetic anchor — no new tab opens, no modal, no confirmation. On failure the red error Alert appears instead.
No row is clickable; there are no row-level action buttons, no edit/delete, no modals, no drawers, no bulk selection, no destructive actions anywhere on this screen.
states: Initial load: both cards render their shells and headings with a centered spinner in place of each table.
Month changed: Card 1 (Monthly Attendance Summary) reverts to its spinner and reloads; Card 2 (Leave Utilization) keeps showing its existing data and does not reload.
Attendance data empty: the table renders with its full 9-column header row and a completely empty body — no 'no data' message (this is a genuine gap in the UI worth reproducing as-is).
Leave data empty: the table renders 'No employees yet.' centered across all columns with py-8.
Error: a red Alert banner appears above the cards showing the backend message; the cards still render below it. A card whose own fetch never resolved stays on its spinner indefinitely.

Permission denied: this route requires the 'reports.view' permission. A user without it never sees the 'Reports' item in the sidebar at all (the menu is built from permissions), and hitting the URL directly surfaces the backend's 403 message inside the red Alert banner.
Session expired (401): the session is cleared and the browser is redirected to /login — the page itself renders nothing.
Narrow viewport: each card scrolls horizontally on its own (overflow-x-auto); the PageHeader wraps so the month navigator and Export button drop onto a second line under the title.

title: Analytics
purpose: A director-level read on company-wide trends: a six-month attendance-rate trend, approved leave split by type and status, headcount by department, and this month's worst late-mark offenders.
layout: Same AppShell chrome as /admin/reports (slate-100 body, fixed left sidebar with the Management section — 'Analytics' is the ACTIVE item here, sitting directly under 'Reports' — plus the top bar). PAGE BODY: (1) PageHeader — flex, flex-wrap, items-center, justify-between, gap-3, mb-6. Left: h1 'Analytics' (text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800) with subtitle 'Company-wide trends across attendance and leave' (text-sm text-slate-500 mt-0.5). Right: a single download button. (2) A responsive grid: `grid grid-cols-1 xl:grid-cols-2 gap-6` — ONE column stacked on anything below the xl breakpoint, TWO equal columns at xl and above. Four cards fill it in this reading order: top-left 'Attendance Rate — last 6 months', top-right 'Approved Leave by Type (days)', bottom-left 'Headcount by Department', bottom-right 'Late Marks — this month'. Every card is `card p-6` (white, rounded-xl, border-slate-200, shadow-sm, 1.5rem padding) and each opens with an h3 in font-bold text-slate-800 mb-4. Cards are not equal height — each sizes to its content. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL NOTE: the loading and error states REPLACE the entire page including the PageHeader — see states.

widgets.label: Download Attendance Report (this month)
widgets.detail: A single btn-secondary in the PageHeader right slot: white bg, border-slate-300, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium, text-slate-700, hover:bg-slate-50, inline-flex items-center gap-2, with a 16px lucide 'Download' icon on the left followed by the literal text 'Download Attendance Report (this month)' (parenthetical included). Always targets the CURRENT calendar month — there is no month picker on this page. Saves as attendance-2026-09.csv.

widgets.label: Attendance Rate — last 6 months (Card 1, top-left)
widgets.detail: Vertical column chart, hand-rolled from divs — no chart library, no axes, no gridlines, no legend, no tooltips. Container: `flex items-end gap-3 h-44` (176px tall, bars grow from a shared baseline). Exactly 6 columns, each `flex-1 flex flex-col items-center justify-end h-full`. Each column top-to-bottom: (a) the value label '87%' in text-xs font-semibold text-slate-700 mb-1, sitting directly above its bar; (b) the bar itself — w-full but capped at max-w-[48px], rounded-t (top corners only), solid bg-brand-600 (#1d4ed8), with inline height set to `max(3, rate)%` of the 176px container so a 0% month still shows a 3% sliver; (c) the x label in text-[11px] text-slate-500 mt-1.5, formatted 'MM/YY' (two-digit month, slash, two-digit year — e.g. '04/26'). Below the chart, a footnote paragraph in text-xs text-slate-400 mt-3 with the exact text: 'Present + WFH (half days count 0.5) as a share of working days.' Months run oldest → newest left to right; each point covers that month's payroll cycle, not the calendar month.

widgets.label: Approved Leave by Type (days) (Card 2, top-right)
widgets.detail: Horizontal bar list in a `space-y-3` stack. Each row (the BarRow component) is `flex items-center gap-3` with three parts: (a) LABEL — the leave type's FULL NAME (not its code), in a fixed `w-28` (7rem) shrink-0 span, text-sm text-slate-600, truncated with ellipsis and carrying the full name as a title tooltip; (b) TRACK — `flex-1 h-5 rounded bg-slate-100` containing a fill div of `h-full rounded bg-purple-500` whose width is `max(2, round(value / maxValue * 100))`% so a zero-day type still shows a 2% stub; (c) VALUE — `w-16` right-aligned span in text-sm font-semibold text-slate-700 showing the day count with no unit suffix. Rows include EVERY configured leave type, including ones with 0 approved days, ordered by leave-type id (creation order). No axis, no gridlines, no tooltips.

widgets.label: Leave status split badge strip (bottom of Card 2)
widgets.detail: A `flex flex-wrap gap-2 mt-5` strip of pill badges directly under the leave-by-type bars, one per distinct leave-application status. Each badge: inline-flex items-center, rounded-full, px-2.5 py-0.5, text-xs font-medium, whitespace-nowrap, with text reading '<Status>: <count>' (e.g. 'Approved: 214'). Colour comes from the status: Approved → bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700; Pending → bg-amber-100 text-amber-700; Rejected → bg-red-100 text-red-700; Cancelled → bg-slate-100 text-slate-600; 'Manager Approved' → bg-blue-100 text-blue-700; 'HR Approved' → bg-purple-100 text-purple-700. Any unrecognised status falls back to slate. The raw status string is shown verbatim — 'Pending' is NOT relabelled here.

widgets.label: Headcount by Department (Card 3, bottom-left)
widgets.detail: The same horizontal BarRow list as Card 2 but with an EMERALD fill (bg-emerald-500) instead of purple: w-28 truncated department name in text-sm text-slate-600, flex-1 h-5 rounded bg-slate-100 track, fill width max(2, round(count/maxCount*100))%, and a w-16 right-aligned text-sm font-semibold text-slate-700 headcount with no suffix. Rows are sorted by headcount DESCENDING. Counts include only Active employees; a department with zero active employees still appears, with a 2% stub bar and the value 0. Stack spacing is space-y-3.

widgets.label: Late Marks — this month (Card 4, bottom-right)
widgets.detail: A ul with `divide-y divide-slate-100`, capped at 5 entries (backend LIMIT 5), sorted by late-mark count descending. Each li is `flex items-center justify-between py-2.5`: LEFT is a text-sm text-slate-700 span with the employee's full name, then a space, then the employee code wrapped in parentheses in text-slate-400 — rendered as 'Ananya Reddy (FTN007)'. RIGHT is an amber pill Badge (bg-amber-100 text-amber-700, rounded-full, px-2.5 py-0.5, text-xs font-medium) reading '<n> late' (e.g. '5 late'). Employees with zero late marks are excluded entirely by the query, so every visible row has at least 1. 'This month' means the running payroll cycle, matching the dashboard counters.

widgets.label: Card 3 empty state
widgets.detail: When no departments exist, the bar list is replaced by a single paragraph in text-sm text-slate-500 reading exactly 'No departments yet.'

widgets.label: Card 4 empty state
widgets.detail: When nobody has a late mark this month, the whole ul is replaced by a paragraph in text-sm text-slate-500 reading exactly 'No late marks recorded this month. 🎉' — the party-popper emoji is part of the string and must be kept.

widgets.label: Full-page loading spinner
widgets.detail: Before data arrives the ENTIRE page is a single Spinner — a centered flex container with py-16 padding holding an 8x8 border-4 border-slate-200 border-t-brand-600 animate-spin circle. The PageHeader, the download button and all four cards are absent during this state (an early return, not a per-card placeholder).

widgets.label: Full-page error alert
widgets.detail: If the analytics fetch fails, the ENTIRE page is replaced by one bare red Alert — rounded-lg, border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50, text-red-700, border-red-200 — containing the backend error message. There is no PageHeader, no download button and no cards behind it, and no retry control. This differs sharply from /admin/reports, where the alert sits above content that still renders.

actions: Click 'Download Attendance Report (this month)': fetches the current calendar month's per-day attendance CSV as an authenticated blob and saves it as attendance-2026-09.csv via a synthetic anchor — no new tab, no modal. On failure the component's error state trips, which (because of the early return) blanks the whole page down to a single red Alert.
Hover a truncated bar label in Card 2 or Card 3: the browser's native title tooltip shows the full leave-type or department name.

Nothing else is interactive: the bars, the badges and the late-mark rows are not clickable; there are no filters, tabs, date pickers, modals, drawers, sorting controls or destructive actions on this screen.
states: Loading: the whole page is one centered spinner — header and cards not rendered.
Error: the whole page is one red Alert with the backend message — header and cards not rendered, no retry button.
Card 3 empty: 'No departments yet.' in text-sm text-slate-500.
Card 4 empty: 'No late marks recorded this month. 🎉' in text-sm text-slate-500.

Zero-value bars: a leave type with 0 approved days or a department with 0 headcount still renders a row, with the fill clamped to a 2% stub so the bar is never invisible; likewise a 0% month in the trend chart renders a 3%-tall sliver.
All-zero data: the bar maths floors the divisor at 1, so a dataset of all zeros renders stub bars rather than dividing by zero or collapsing.

Responsive: below the xl breakpoint the 2-column grid collapses to a single column and the four cards stack in order (trend, leave by type, headcount, late marks); the PageHeader wraps so the download button drops below the title.

Permission denied: this route requires the 'analytics.view' permission. Without it the 'Analytics' item is absent from the sidebar entirely, and visiting the URL directly renders the full-page red Alert carrying the backend's 403 message.
Session expired (401): session cleared and redirected to /login.

title: Document Management
purpose: One admin screen with three tabs for uploading, generating, viewing, replacing and deleting employee salary slips, company policies and offer letters; this tab (Salary Slips, the default) lists every slip for one selected employee and lets the admin generate a new slip from amounts or upload a ready-made PDF.
layout:
NOTE FOR THE MOCKUP BUILDER: all three tabs live at the single real URL /admin/documents — the tab is React state (useState(TABS[0])), not a route. Render them as one page with a working tab strip, or as three pages of one screen. 

APP SHELL (from components/AppShell.jsx, wrapping every /admin page): fixed left sidebar 256px wide (w-64), background slate-900, hidden below lg and replaced by a hamburger + slide-over with a slate-900/60 backdrop. Sidebar top: F1HR logo image (light variant, 30px tall) with a bottom border border-slate-800, px-5 py-5. Below it a company block: px-5 py-2.5, border-b border-slate-800, tiny uppercase label 'COMPANY' in text-slate-500 at 11px, then the company name in text-sm font-semibold text-slate-200. Then the nav (flex-1, overflow-y-auto, px-3 py-4, space-y-1). For an admin/HR user the nav shows a section heading 'MANAGEMENT' (11px, semibold, uppercase, tracking-wider, text-slate-500, px-3 pb-1) followed by links: Overview (/admin, LayoutDashboard icon), Employees (/admin/employees, Users), Attendance (/admin/attendance, CalendarClock), Leave Management (/admin/leaves, ClipboardCheck), Leave Balances (/admin/balances, Calculator), Documents (/admin/documents, FolderOpen), Reports (/admin/reports, BarChart3), Analytics (/admin/analytics, LineChart), Settings (/admin/settings, Settings), Email Log (/admin/emails, Mails). Each link: flex, gap-3, rounded-lg, px-3 py-2.5, text-sm font-medium; inactive text-slate-300 hover:bg-slate-800 hover:text-white; ACTIVE (Documents here) bg-brand-600 text-white. Below Management a standalone 'Change Password' link (KeyRound icon). Sidebar footer: border-t border-slate-800, p-3, full-width 'Logout' button (LogOut icon) text-slate-300 hover:bg-red-600/90 hover:text-white.

MAIN COLUMN: lg:pl-64. Sticky top header, bg-white, border-b border-slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8, py-3, flex justify-between. Left: hamburger (lg:hidden) then a muted line 'FOne HR — <company name>' in text-sm text-slate-500 (hidden on xs). Right: the user block — right-aligned two lines, name in text-sm font-semibold text-slate-800 and beneath it text-xs text-slate-500 showing '<ROLE> · <EMP CODE>' — followed by a 36px circular avatar, bg-brand-600, white bold initials. (The notification bell only renders for non-admin users, so it is absent on admin screens.) Main content area: <main className='p-4 lg:p-8'>. Page background is slate-100.

PAGE BODY, top to bottom:
1. PageHeader: h1 'Document Management' (text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800) with subtitle beneath it 'Upload, replace and delete salary slips, policies and offer letters' (text-sm text-slate-500, mt-0.5). mb-6.
2. Conditional alert banner slot (mb-4) — error (red) or success (green), see states.
3. Tab strip: flex gap-2 mb-6, three buttons.
4. Tab body (Salary Slips): a white .card, p-4 mb-4, flex flex-wrap items-end gap-4 — an Employee <select> in a 260px-min column, then the 'Generate Slip' primary button, then the 'Upload PDF Slip' secondary button, all bottom-aligned.
5. Below it a white .card with overflow-x-auto containing the salary-slips table (full width, thead bg-slate-50, rows divided by slate-100).
6. Two modals rendered on demand, centred, over a slate-900/50 backdrop.

widgets.label: Page header

widgets.label: Employee selector + action bar (white card)

widgets.label: Per-row action buttons

widgets.label: Generate Salary Slip modal

Body is a 2-column grid (grid-cols-2 gap-4) containing 13 fields in this exact order: [1] 'MONTH' — <select>, 12 options January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December (values 1–12), defaults to the current month; [2] 'YEAR' — <input type=number>, required, defaults to the current year; [3] 'BASIC (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [4] 'HRA (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [5] 'SPECIAL ALLOWANCE (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [6] 'CONVEYANCE (₹)' — number, min 0, required, defaults to 1600; [7] 'PF DEDUCTION (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [8] 'TAX (TDS) (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [9] 'LOP DEDUCTION (₹)' — number, min 0, required; [10] 'PAN NUMBER' — text, optional; [11] 'BANK NAME' — text, optional; [12] 'BANK ACCOUNT NO.' — text, optional; [13] 'BANK IFSC' — text, optional. PRE-FILL BEHAVIOUR worth showing in the mockup: opening the modal copies the amounts from the employee's most recent slip that has amounts, and the PAN/bank fields from the employee record, so the fields open populated rather than blank. Net pay is NOT shown in this form — it is computed server-side as basic + hra + special_allowance + conveyance − pf_deduction − tax_deduction − lop_deduction.

widgets.label: Upload Salary Slip PDF modal

Body is a vertical stack (space-y-4): (a) explanatory paragraph in text-sm text-slate-500 reading 'Upload a ready-made slip for <EMP CODE>. It replaces the generated one for that month if a slip already exists.' where the emp code is bold/slate-700 inline; (b) a 2-column grid with 'MONTH' (<select>, same 12 month options, defaults to current month) and 'YEAR' (<input type=number>, required, defaults to current year); (c) 'PDF FILE' — <input type=file accept='application/pdf'> styled with the .input class, required. Footer: right-aligned 'Cancel' (btn-secondary) and 'Upload' (btn-primary, submit).

actions: Click tab 'Salary Slips' / 'Company Policies' / 'Offer Letters' — swaps the tab body in place; the URL does not change.
Change the Employee dropdown — clears the table to a spinner and reloads that employee's slips.
'Generate Slip' — opens the Generate Salary Slip modal pre-filled from the last slip with amounts plus the employee's PAN/bank details.
'Upload PDF Slip' — opens the Upload Salary Slip PDF modal defaulted to the current month and year.

Row Eye icon ('View PDF') — fetches the slip as a blob and opens it in a new tab; if the slip has neither amounts nor an uploaded file the red error banner appears reading 'This slip has neither amounts nor an uploaded PDF'.

Row Trash2 icon ('Delete') — DESTRUCTIVE. Fires a native browser confirm() reading 'Delete salary slip September 2026?' (the period label is interpolated); on OK the slip is deleted, a green banner reads 'Salary slip deleted' and the table reloads.

Modal 'Generate' — submits; on success the modal closes, a green banner reads 'Salary slip generated' and the table reloads. Duplicate period returns the red banner 'A slip for that employee/month already exists'.
Modal 'Upload' — submits the multipart form; green banner reads 'Salary slip PDF uploaded', or 'Slip PDF replaced' when a slip for that period already existed.
Modal 'Cancel', the '×' button, or a click on the dark backdrop — closes the modal without saving.
states: Initial load: the employee list is fetched first; until an employee is selected the table area is empty. Once selected, rows are null and a Spinner renders — a centred 32px circle, border-4 border-slate-200 with a brand-600 top border, animate-spin, inside a flex justify-center py-16 block.

Empty: when the selected employee has no slips the table renders its header row plus a single full-width row spanning all 5 columns reading 'No salary slips for this employee.' centred, text-slate-500, py-8. (Only the Salary Slips tab has this empty row — the other two tabs render an empty tbody.)
Loading after any mutation: delete / generate / upload each reset rows to null, so the Spinner replaces the table again between the action and the refreshed list.
Error: any failed request replaces the banner slot with the red Alert carrying the server's error text; the success banner is cleared at the same time. Errors do NOT auto-dismiss.
Success: green Alert, clears itself after 4 seconds; the error banner is cleared at the same time.

Permission denied: the whole screen is gated on the 'documents.manage' permission — without it the 'Documents' entry never appears in the Management sidebar section, and a direct hit on the API returns 403 which surfaces as the red banner 'Not allowed'.
Session expired: a 401 from any call clears the stored session and hard-redirects to /login. Fifteen minutes of no mouse/keyboard/scroll activity logs the user out to /login?timeout=1.
Conditional: the Net Pay cell shows '—' instead of a rupee amount for slips that exist only as an uploaded PDF with no entered amounts.
Conditional: the Source badge is purple 'Uploaded PDF' when a file backs the slip, blue 'Generated' otherwise.
Responsive: below lg the sidebar collapses behind a hamburger; the table card scrolls horizontally; the filter card wraps its controls onto multiple lines.

title: My Attendance
purpose: Lets a logged-in employee review their own attendance for one month — six summary counters, a colour-coded day grid, and a day-by-day table with biometric entry/exit times.
layout: Rendered inside AppShell (app/(employee)/layout.jsx). SHELL: fixed dark sidebar on the left, 256px wide (w-64, bg-slate-900), visible only at lg+; below lg it is hidden and opens as an overlay drawer from a hamburger. Main column is offset lg:pl-64. At the top of the main column a sticky white header bar (bg-white, border-b border-slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8, py-3) with left = hamburger (mobile only) + muted text 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd', right = notification bell with red unread badge, then a right-aligned two-line name/role block, then a 36px circular brand-blue avatar with initials. Page body is <main class='p-4 lg:p-8'> on a bg-slate-100 page background. PAGE CONTENT top-to-bottom, four blocks: (1) PageHeader — a flex row, flex-wrap, justify-between, gap-3, mb-6; left side is an h1 'My Attendance' (text-2xl, bold, slate-800) with the subtitle 'Daily and monthly attendance overview' (text-sm, slate-500, mt-0.5) beneath it; right side holds the MonthPicker. (2) Stat grid — grid gap-4 mb-6, 2 columns on mobile, 3 at sm, 6 at xl; exactly six cards, in fixed order Working Days, Present, Absent, Half Days, WFH, Late Marks. (3) Calendar card — white .card (rounded-xl, border-slate-200, shadow-sm) with p-6; inside it an h3 'Attendance Calendar' (font-bold, slate-800, mb-4) then the AttendanceCalendar: a 7-column weekday header strip (gap-1.5, text-center, text-xs, font-semibold, slate-500, mb-2), then a 7-column day grid (gap-1.5) of equal cells, then a flex-wrap legend row (gap-2, mt-4). (4) Detail table card — a second .card with mt-6 and overflow-x-auto wrapping a full-width table (min-w-full, divide-y divide-slate-200) with a bg-slate-50 header row and rows separated by divide-slate-100. There is NO footer, NO pagination, NO export button and NO modal on this screen. Nothing on this screen shows money.

widgets.label: Sidebar navigation (AppShell chrome)
widgets.detail: Dark slate-900 column. Top: logo block (px-5 py-5, border-b border-slate-800) with the light FOne HR logo. Then a company strip (px-5 py-2.5, border-b border-slate-800): tiny uppercase slate-500 caption 'Company' above the company name in text-sm font-semibold slate-200. Then the nav (flex-1, overflow-y-auto, px-3 py-4, space-y-1) built from the employee's permissions, as collapsible groups: group 'Home' (Home icon) containing 'Home' (/home) and 'Dashboard' (/dashboard); group 'Attendance & Leave' (CalendarCheck icon) containing 'Attendance' (/attendance), 'Leave Balance' (/leave/balance), 'Apply Leave' (/leave/apply), 'Leave History' (/leave/history), and — only with the leaves.approve permission — 'Approvals' (/leave/approvals); group 'Documents' (FolderOpen icon) containing 'Salary Slips' (/documents/salary-slips), 'Offer Letter' (/documents/offer-letter), 'Company Policies' (/documents/policies); then a flat item 'Change Password' (/change-password, KeyRound icon). A group auto-expands when the current path is inside it, so on this screen 'Attendance & Leave' is OPEN and its child 'Attendance' is the active item, rendered bg-brand-600 (#1d4ed8) with white text; siblings are slate-400 on transparent. Group children sit indented (ml-4, pl-3) behind a left border-slate-700 rail. Bottom, below a border-t border-slate-800: a full-width 'Logout' button (LogOut icon, slate-300, hover turns red).

widgets.label: Top header bar (AppShell chrome)
widgets.detail: Left: hamburger Menu icon (lg:hidden) then the text 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' (text-sm, slate-500, hidden below sm). Right cluster (gap-5): (a) notification Bell button, 20px, in a rounded-full hover:bg-slate-100 hit area, with an absolute -top-1 -right-1 red-500 pill badge showing the unread count in 9px bold white with a white ring — hidden when the count is 0; (b) a right-aligned text block — line 1 the employee's full name (text-sm, font-semibold, slate-800), line 2 'ROLE · EMPCODE' (text-xs, slate-500), e.g. 'EMPLOYEE · FTN042'; (c) a 36px rounded-full bg-brand-600 avatar with the first letters of the first two name words, uppercase, in white text-sm bold.

widgets.label: Month Picker (MonthPicker, in the PageHeader right slot)
widgets.detail: A single inline row, flex items-center gap-2, of exactly three elements. LEFT: a button with the literal glyph '←' (HTML ←), styled .btn-secondary with !px-3 — white background, border-slate-300, slate-700 text, rounded-lg, text-sm. CENTRE: a span with min-w-[150px] and text-center containing up to two stacked lines — line 1 is the month name and year from the en-US long-month format, e.g. 'August 2026' (block, text-sm, font-semibold, slate-700); line 2 is the payroll-period range label from the API, e.g. '25 Jul – 24 Aug 2026' (block, text-[11px], slate-400, leading-tight) and it is rendered ONLY when that label differs from line 1. With the current backend the attendance grid is a plain calendar month, so the API returns the label 'August 2026', it matches line 1, and line 2 is NOT drawn — the picker shows a single line. RIGHT: a button with the glyph '→' (HTML →), same .btn-secondary !px-3 styling. No dropdown, no year selector, no date input — stepping is one month at a time only.

widgets.label: Working Days
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered exactly as 'WORKING DAYS' (source text 'Working Days'; the class forces uppercase, text-xs, font-semibold, tracking-wide, slate-500). Value is a bare integer count of days with no unit suffix (text-2xl, font-bold, slate-800). Icon: lucide Briefcase at 22px, in a rounded-lg p-2.5 tile using the DEFAULT brand tint — text-brand-600 on bg-brand-50 (blue #1d4ed8 on #f0f6ff). Card is .card p-5, flex items-start gap-4. Counts every date in the month that is neither a Saturday/Sunday nor a company holiday. No sub-line.

widgets.label: Present
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered as 'PRESENT'. Value is a bare integer day count, no unit. Icon: lucide CalendarCheck, 22px, tile text-emerald-600 on bg-emerald-50. Counts only records whose status is exactly 'Present' — WFH, Half Day, EL, SL and LOP days are NOT included here. Same .card p-5 flex layout. No sub-line.

widgets.label: Absent
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered as 'ABSENT'. Value is a bare integer day count, no unit. Icon: lucide CalendarX, 22px, tile text-red-600 on bg-red-50. Counts only status exactly 'Absent'. No sub-line.

widgets.label: Half Days
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered as 'HALF DAYS'. Value is a bare integer day count, no unit. Icon: lucide SunMedium, 22px, tile text-amber-600 on bg-amber-50. Counts only status exactly 'Half Day'. No sub-line.

widgets.label: WFH
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered as 'WFH' (already an acronym; stays uppercase). Value is a bare integer day count, no unit. Icon: lucide Laptop, 22px, tile text-cyan-600 on bg-cyan-50. Counts only status exactly 'WFH'. No sub-line.

widgets.label: Late Marks
widgets.detail: Metric label rendered as 'LATE MARKS'. Value is a bare integer count of DAYS flagged late (not minutes, not a percentage), no unit suffix. Icon: lucide Clock3, 22px, tile text-orange-600 on bg-orange-50. Counts every record carrying the late_mark flag regardless of its status. No sub-line. IMPORTANT QUIRK to reproduce: there is no stat card for leave. Days marked 'Leave', 'EL', 'SL' or 'LOP' are drawn on the calendar and listed in the table but are counted by NONE of these six cards, so the five day-type cards will not add up to Working Days whenever such days exist.

widgets.label: Attendance Calendar (AttendanceCalendar component)
widgets.detail: HEADER STRIP: seven equal columns, labels exactly 'Sun','Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu','Fri','Sat' (text-center, text-xs, font-semibold, slate-500). GRID: grid-cols-7 gap-1.5. It draws the API's date range, not a hard-coded 1-to-31 month; the range currently equals the calendar month. Leading empty <div> pad cells fill the columns before the first date's weekday — for August 2026 the 1st is a Saturday, so there are SIX blank pads and Aug 1 sits alone in the last column of row 1. DAY CELL: a <button>, rounded-lg, 1px border, p-1.5 (sm:p-2), min-h-[52px] (sm:min-h-[64px]), text-left, with up to five stacked pieces — (1) the day number in text-xs font-bold, optionally followed by a short month name (ml-1, font-semibold, opacity-70) which appears ONLY on the very first cell of the grid and on any cell that is the 1st of a month (so August 2026 shows 'Aug' on the 1st cell and nowhere else); (2) the status text in text-[10px] sm:text-xs font-medium mt-0.5 — on mobile the SHORT CODE, at sm and above the FULL LABEL; (3) the holiday name, sm-and-above only, text-[9px] font-normal, truncated to one line; (4) the biometric times line, text-[9px] sm:text-[10px], font-normal, opacity-80, tabular-nums, truncated, rendered only when an entry or exit time exists, formatted '19:04 – 04:12' (en dash, spaces) and collapsing to just the entry time when there is no exit time or the two are identical; (5) the word 'Late' on its own line in text-[9px] text-red-600 when the day is flagged late. TEN STATUS COLOURS (background / text / border, all Tailwind 100/800/200 unless noted): Present = emerald; WFH = cyan; Half Day = amber; Absent = red; Leave = purple; EL = violet; SL = orange; LOP = rose; Holiday = blue; Weekend = slate-100 background with muted slate-400 text and slate-200 border. SHORT CODES, in the same order: P, W, H, A, L, EL, SL, LOP, HO, and an em dash '—' for Weekend. FULL DESKTOP LABELS: Present, WFH, Half Day, Absent, Leave, and — spelled out rather than coded — 'Earned Leave' for EL, 'Sick Leave' for SL, 'Loss of Pay' for LOP, then Holiday, Weekend. UNRECOGNISED STATUS: falls back to bg-slate-100 text-slate-700 border-slate-300 and prints the raw status string, so it is never invisible. NO RECORD, date in the past or today: bg-white, border-slate-200, slate-400 day number, empty body. NO RECORD, future date: bg-slate-50/50, border-slate-100, slate-300 day number, and the body shows the italic word 'Locked' in text-[9px] slate-300 at sm and above only (blank on mobile). TOOLTIP (native title attribute): the holiday name if the day has one, otherwise the full status label, otherwise 'Future date (locked)' on a future day, otherwise nothing. INTERACTION ON THIS SCREEN: the employee page passes no day-click handler, so every cell is inert — cursor-default and opacity-85 throughout, with no hover ring. (The same component gains hover:ring-2 hover:ring-brand-500 and cursor-pointer on non-future days when a handler is supplied, which is how the admin screen uses it; do not show that here.)

widgets.label: Status legend (below the calendar grid)
widgets.detail: A flex-wrap row, gap-2, mt-4, of exactly ten chips in this fixed order: Present, WFH, Half Day, Absent, Leave, Earned Leave, Sick Leave, Loss of Pay, Holiday, Weekend. Note the last five words: EL, SL and LOP are spelled out in the legend even though the mobile cells show the codes. Each chip is inline-flex items-center, rounded-md, 1px border, px-2 py-0.5, text-xs, font-medium, and carries the exact same background/text/border colour trio as its calendar cells (emerald, cyan, amber, red, purple, violet, orange, rose, blue, slate). The legend is always fully rendered — it lists every status the system can produce, not just the ones present in the displayed month.

widgets.label: Attendance detail table
widgets.detail: Exactly five columns, left-aligned, in this order: 'Date', 'Status', 'Entry Time', 'Exit Time', 'Late'. Header cells: px-4 py-3, text-left, text-xs, font-semibold, UPPERCASE, tracking-wider, slate-500, on a bg-slate-50 thead. Body cells: px-4 py-3, text-sm; rows get hover:bg-slate-50 and are separated by divide-slate-100. COLUMN CONTENT — Date: rendered DD/MM/YYYY (e.g. '03/08/2026'), font-medium. Status: the raw status string ('Present', 'WFH', 'Half Day', 'Absent', 'Leave', 'EL', 'SL', 'LOP'), plain text with NO coloured badge or pill, or an em dash '—' when the record has no status. Entry Time: 24-hour HH:MM, or '—'. Exit Time: 24-hour HH:MM, or '—'. Late: the word 'Yes' in text-red-600 font-medium when flagged, otherwise a plain 'No'. ROW FILTER (critical): rows whose status is 'Weekend' or 'Holiday' are excluded entirely, so the table lists only working-day records — it is shorter than the calendar and skips Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. Days that carry biometric punches but were never marked by HR are NOT filtered out; they appear with '—' in Status but real Entry/Exit times. Rows are in ascending date order. No row actions, no checkboxes, no sorting controls, no pagination, and no empty-state message — when there is nothing to show only the header row remains.

actions: '←' button in the Month Picker: steps back one month; at January it wraps to December of the previous year. Clears the loaded data first, so the whole content area drops to the spinner before the new month paints.

'→' button in the Month Picker: steps forward one month; at December it wraps to January of the next year. There is no upper limit — you can page into future months, which render an all-'Locked' grid and zeroed stat cards.
Calendar day cells: they are real <button> elements but this screen passes no click handler, so clicking one does nothing (cursor-default, opacity-85, no hover ring, no drawer, no modal).
Sidebar group headers ('Home', 'Attendance & Leave', 'Documents'): toggle open/closed, rotating the chevron 180 degrees.
Sidebar links: plain navigation to the listed routes.
'Logout' in the sidebar footer: clears the stored session and redirects to /login. Destructive to the session only; there is no confirmation prompt.

Notification bell in the header: toggles a 320px dropdown anchored right, listing notification cards (title, two-line clamped body, timestamp as DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS), with a 'Mark all as read' link in its header when there are unread ones and a 'View all notifications' bar at the bottom that opens the full notification drawer. Opening the bell does NOT mark anything read; opening an individual card does.
No export, download, print, edit, regularisation, apply-leave or delete action exists anywhere on this screen — it is strictly read-only.
states: LOADING: while the month is being fetched the PageHeader and Month Picker stay visible and everything below them is replaced by a single centred spinner — a 32px circle, 4px border, border-slate-200 with a brand-blue top edge, spinning, inside a py-16 flex-centred block. This appears on first mount AND again on every month change, because the data is cleared before each fetch.

ERROR: if the request fails the ENTIRE page is replaced by one alert box and nothing else renders — no heading, no month picker, no stats, no calendar, no table. The alert is a rounded-lg box with a 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200, containing the raw server message. It is terminal: there is no retry button and the state never clears, so the user must reload.

ERROR TEXT to use in a mockup: 'No employee profile linked to this account' — the real 400 returned when the signed-in login has no employee record attached (this is also what a platform-admin account hitting this route sees). An expired token instead silently clears the session and bounces to /login.

EMPTY MONTH (no attendance ever recorded): all six stat values show 0 except Working Days, which still counts weekdays; the calendar draws every weekday as a plain white cell with just its day number, with only Saturdays/Sundays in muted slate and any holidays in blue; the table renders its header row with an empty body and NO 'no records' message.

FUTURE MONTH: every non-weekend cell is pale (bg-slate-50/50, border-slate-100, slate-300 number) and shows the italic word 'Locked' at sm and above, with the tooltip 'Future date (locked)'. Stat cards read 0 apart from Working Days.
PARTIAL MONTH (the normal live case): days up to today are filled, later weekdays are 'Locked'.

NO BIOMETRIC DEVICE: for a company without device attendance the entry/exit times are never fetched, so the 'Entry Time' and 'Exit Time' columns show '—' on every row and the calendar cells carry no times line at all. Everything else is unchanged.

UNMARKED PUNCH DAY: a day the biometric device recorded but HR never marked appears with a blank/uncoloured calendar cell that still shows its times line, and as a table row with '—' in the Status column but real Entry and Exit times. Worth including one such row in the mockup.

UNKNOWN STATUS: any status the calendar does not recognise still renders, in neutral slate (bg-slate-100 / text-slate-700 / border-slate-300) with the raw string as its label, rather than a blank cell.

PERIOD SUB-LABEL: the second line under the month name in the picker is conditional and currently inert — the attendance grid is a calendar month so the API's period label equals the month name and the line is suppressed. It would appear (e.g. '25 Jul – 24 Aug 2026') only if the grid were switched back to the 25th-to-24th payroll cycle, in which case the grid would also span two calendar months and show a 'Jul' month tag on its first cell plus an 'Aug' tag on the 1st.

MOBILE (below sm): the sidebar collapses behind a hamburger and opens as an overlay drawer with a dark scrim; stat cards drop to two per row; calendar cells shrink to min-h-[52px] and show only the SHORT CODE (P/W/H/A/L/EL/SL/LOP/HO/—) instead of the full label, with holiday names and the 'Locked' text hidden entirely; the detail table scrolls horizontally inside its card.
NO PERMISSION-DENIED STATE: this route is available to every employee login and is not permission-gated, so there is no 'access denied' screen to design.
IDLE TIMEOUT: after 15 minutes without mouse, keyboard, click, scroll or touch activity the session is cleared and the user is redirected to /login?timeout=1.

title: Salary Slips
purpose: Lets a logged-in employee browse every month-wise salary slip issued to them and open, download or print the PDF for any one of them.
layout: Shared employee app shell wraps the page. LEFT: fixed dark sidebar, width 256px (w-64), background slate-900, full height, z-30, hidden below the lg breakpoint (1024px) where it becomes an overlay drawer. MAIN COLUMN: offset by 256px on lg+ (lg:pl-64); contains a sticky white top header bar (height ~56px, border-bottom slate-200, padding px-4 lg:px-8 py-3, z-20) and below it the page body with padding p-4 on mobile / p-8 on lg+. Page background is slate-100; all cards are white. PAGE BODY top-to-bottom: (1) PageHeader block — flex row, wrap, items-center, justify-between, gap-3, margin-bottom 24px; left side holds an h1 'Salary Slips' at text-2xl font-bold slate-800 and directly under it a subtitle 'View, download or print your month-wise salary slips' at text-sm slate-500 with mt-0.5; there is NO right-hand action slot on this page (no filter, no year picker, no export button). (2) A responsive card grid immediately below: CSS grid, gap 16px, 1 column on mobile, 2 columns from the sm breakpoint (640px), 3 columns from the xl breakpoint (1280px). Every slip is one card; cards are equal width and stretch to equal height within a row (each card is itself a flex column). There is no table anywhere on this screen. When the list is loading the PageHeader is NOT rendered at all — the entire page body is replaced by a centred spinner. When an error occurs the PageHeader is likewise NOT rendered — the entire page body is replaced by a single red alert strip.

widgets.label: Sidebar navigation (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Dark slate-900 column, 256px wide. Top block: px-5 py-5, bottom border slate-800, contains the F1HR logo image (light variant, rendered 30px tall, width auto, roughly 95x30) and, below lg, an X close button in slate-400 on its right. Next block: px-5 py-2.5, bottom border slate-800 — an 11px uppercase tracking-wide slate-500 label reading 'COMPANY' and under it the company name in text-sm font-semibold slate-200, truncated ('Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd'). Then a scrollable <nav> with px-3 py-4 and 4px vertical spacing between items. For a plain (non-admin) employee the items, in exact order, are: [collapsible group] 'Home' with a Home icon, children 'Home' (/home, Home icon) and 'Dashboard' (/dashboard, LayoutDashboard icon); [collapsible group] 'Attendance & Leave' with a CalendarCheck icon, children 'Attendance' (/attendance, CalendarCheck), 'Leave Balance' (/leave/balance, Scale), 'Apply Leave' (/leave/apply, FilePlus2), 'Leave History' (/leave/history, History), and — only when the user holds the leaves.approve permission — 'Approvals' (/leave/approvals, ClipboardCheck); [collapsible group] 'Documents' with a FolderOpen icon, children 'Salary Slips' (/documents/salary-slips, FileText), 'Offer Letter' (/documents/offer-letter, FileBadge), 'Company Policies' (/documents/policies, BookOpen); then, only when the user holds documents.manage, a flat link 'Payroll' (/admin/payroll, Banknote icon); then, only when the user holds management permissions, a section captioned 'MANAGEMENT' (11px uppercase tracking-wider slate-500, px-3 pb-1, pt-3 above) listing any of Overview, Employees, Attendance, Leave Management, Leave Balances, Documents, Reports, Analytics, Settings, Email Log, Roles & Access; finally a flat link 'Change Password' (/change-password, KeyRound icon). Group headers are full-width buttons with the group icon + label on the left and a ChevronDown 16px on the right that rotates 180 degrees when open; a group auto-opens if the current path is one of its children. Child links sit in an indented rail: ml-4, mt-1, left border slate-700, pl-3. Link styling: top-level rounded-lg px-3 py-2.5 text-sm font-medium, inactive slate-300 with hover bg-slate-800 + white text; ACTIVE link is solid brand-600 (#1d4ed8) with white text. Child links are rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm, inactive slate-400, active brand-600 background with white font-medium text. On this screen the 'Documents' group is expanded and the 'Salary Slips' child is the active brand-600 pill. Footer: top border slate-800, p-3, a full-width 'Logout' button (LogOut icon 18px) in slate-300 that turns red-600/90 background with white text on hover.

widgets.label: Top header bar (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Sticky white bar, bottom border slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8, py-3, flex justify-between items-center. LEFT: a hamburger Menu icon (22px, slate-600) shown only below lg, then a text-sm slate-500 line hidden below the sm breakpoint reading 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' (the em-dash and company name are literal). RIGHT (flex, gap 20px): (a) a notification bell — Bell icon 20px slate-500 in a 1.5 padding rounded-full hover:bg-slate-100 button, with a red-500 unread-count pill absolutely positioned at its top-right (-top-1 -right-1, height 16px, min-width 16px, rounded-full, 9px bold white text, 2px white ring) shown only when there is at least one unread notification; (b) a right-aligned two-line identity block — line 1 'Sneha Iyer' in text-sm font-semibold slate-800, line 2 in text-xs slate-500 reading role then a middle dot then the employee code, e.g. 'EMPLOYEE · FTN0042'; (c) a 36px circular avatar, background brand-600, white text-sm font-bold, showing the first letters of the first two words of the display name, uppercased — 'SI'.

widgets.label: Notification bell dropdown (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Opens on bell click, anchored to the bell's right edge, mt-2, width 320px, rounded-xl, border slate-200, white, shadow-lg, z-50, overflow hidden. Header strip: px-4 py-2.5, bg-slate-50, bottom border, left 'Notifications' in 12px bold slate-700, right a 'Mark all as read' link in 11px font-semibold brand-600 with hover underline, shown only when unreadCount > 0. Body: max-height 256px, scrollable, rows divided by slate-100. Each row: px-4 py-3, cursor pointer, hover bg-slate-50, unread rows tinted brand-50/30; inside, a flex row with the notification title (text-xs font-semibold, slate-800 when unread / slate-600 when read) and, for unread rows only, a 6px brand-500 dot on the right; under it the body clamped to 2 lines in 11px slate-500; under that the timestamp in 9px slate-400 formatted DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS. Empty state: 'No notifications yet.' centred, px-4 py-8, 12px italic slate-400. Footer, only when there is at least one notification: a full-width 'View all notifications' button, top border slate-200, bg-slate-50, px-4 py-2.5, 11px font-semibold brand-600. Clicking a row closes the dropdown, marks that one read, and opens the right-hand drawer scrolled to that notification.

widgets.label: Notification reader drawer (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: A right-side slide-in drawer (200ms transition) holding the full notification list as expandable cards. Each card: rounded-xl white with a slate-200 border, a 4px brand-500 left border while unread, and a brand-500 border plus shadow while expanded. Card header is a button, px-4 py-3, hover bg-slate-50: title in text-sm (font-bold slate-900 when unread, font-semibold slate-700 when read), a 6px brand-500 dot for unread, a 2-line clamped preview in text-xs slate-500 shown only while collapsed, the timestamp in 11px slate-400, and a ChevronDown 16px on the right that rotates when expanded. Expanded body: top border slate-100, px-4 py-3, full body text in text-sm leading-relaxed slate-700 with whitespace preserved, plus — only if the notification carries a link — an 'Open' button with a right-arrow icon in 12px font-semibold brand-600. The drawer also offers 'Mark all read' (CheckCheck icon) and a close X.

widgets.label: Salary slip card grid
widgets.detail: The only content widget on the page. A CSS grid with gap 16px: grid-cols-1 / sm:grid-cols-2 / xl:grid-cols-3. One card per salary slip, ordered newest first (year descending, then month descending). Each card is class 'card' — white, rounded-xl, 1px slate-200 border, small shadow — with padding 20px (p-5) and laid out as a flex column so every card in a row is the same height and the button row sits flush at the bottom. CARD CONTENT, top to bottom: (1) An identity row: flex, items-center, gap 12px. Left is a square icon tile, rounded-lg, padding 10px, background brand-50 (#f0f6ff), holding a lucide 'FileText' icon at 22px in brand-600 (#1d4ed8). Right is a two-line text block: line 1 is the slip label in font-semibold slate-800, always the full month name and year of the payroll cycle, e.g. 'August 2026'; line 2 is text-xs slate-500 and is CONDITIONAL — when the slip has a net_pay value it reads the literal words 'Net Pay: ' followed by the amount wrapped in font-medium slate-700, and when net_pay is null it instead reads the flat string 'Salary slip document'. (2) A button row: flex, gap 8px, margin-top 16px, three buttons each flex-1 so they split the card width equally, each class btn-secondary with horizontal padding forced down to 8px (white background, 1px slate-300 border, slate-700 text, rounded-lg, py-2, text-sm font-medium, gap-2, hover bg-slate-50) — button 1 is an Eye icon at 15px plus the word 'View', button 2 is a Download icon at 15px plus the word 'PDF', button 3 is a Printer icon at 15px plus the word 'Print' and carries the native tooltip 'Opens PDF — use the browser print option'. AMOUNT FORMAT: a rupee sign immediately followed by the number rendered with Indian digit grouping and NO decimal places and NO space — e.g. ₹61,480 and ₹1,02,450. NOTE FOR THE MOCKUP: the API also returns a 'period' string (e.g. '25 Jul – 24 Aug 2026') and a 'source' flag ('uploaded' or 'generated') but this page renders NEITHER — do not display a date range or a source chip on these cards.

widgets.label: Info alert — empty list
widgets.detail: Rendered only when the employee has zero slips. Class: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, colours bg-blue-50 / text-blue-700 / border-blue-200. Copy is exactly 'No salary slips available yet.'. It is emitted as the FIRST CHILD OF THE GRID, so it occupies a single grid cell (one column wide) rather than spanning the full page width.

widgets.label: Error alert — request failure
widgets.detail: Rendered INSTEAD OF the entire page (no PageHeader, no grid) whenever the list fetch or any View/PDF/Print fetch fails. Class: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, colours bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200. Text is the raw server error message. Realistic strings: 'No employee profile linked to this account', 'Salary slip not found', 'File missing on server', 'Failed to fetch document', 'Request failed'. There is no dismiss button and no retry button — the page stays on the alert until reloaded.

widgets.label: Loading spinner
widgets.detail: Shown while the slip list is still in flight, again INSTEAD OF the entire page including the PageHeader. A flex container centred horizontally with 64px vertical padding (py-16) holding a single 32px circle: rounded-full, 4px border in slate-200 with the top border in brand-600, continuously spinning.

actions: View (Eye icon, first button on each card) — fetches GET /api/documents/salary-slips/{id}/pdf with the bearer token, turns the response into a blob URL and opens it in a NEW BROWSER TAB. It does not open an in-app modal or preview pane.
PDF (Download icon, second button) — same authenticated fetch, then triggers a hidden anchor download named salary-slip-{Label-with-first-space-hyphenated}.pdf, e.g. 'salary-slip-August-2026.pdf'.

Print (Printer icon, third button) — behaves IDENTICALLY to View: it opens the same PDF in a new tab and relies on the browser's own print command. No print dialog, no print stylesheet, no separate print route.
Any of the three failing replaces the whole page with the red error alert (destructive to the current view, though nothing is deleted).

Sidebar: expand/collapse the Home, Attendance & Leave and Documents groups; navigate to any child route; 'Change Password'; 'Logout' (clears the stored token and user from localStorage and redirects to /login).

Header: hamburger opens the mobile sidebar overlay (a slate-900/60 scrim plus the 256px drawer; tapping the scrim or the X closes it); bell toggles the notification dropdown and refetches notifications; 'Mark all as read' in the dropdown; clicking a notification row opens the reader drawer with that item expanded and marks it read; 'View all notifications' opens the drawer with nothing pre-expanded; 'Open' inside an expanded notification navigates to its linked route and closes the drawer.

This page has NO destructive actions — an employee cannot delete, upload or regenerate a slip. Deleting and creating slips lives on the admin Payroll/Documents screens behind the documents.manage permission.
states: Loading — rows is null: the PageHeader is suppressed and the body is only the centred spinner.
Loaded with data — PageHeader plus the responsive card grid.
Empty — PageHeader plus a single blue info alert 'No salary slips available yet.' sitting in the first grid cell.
Error — the PageHeader is suppressed and the body is only the red alert carrying the server message; no retry affordance.

Conditional per card — when net_pay is null the sub-line falls back from 'Net Pay: ₹…' to the plain text 'Salary slip document' (this is the case for slips uploaded as ready-made PDFs rather than generated from amounts).

Permission — no gate on this route: every non-admin user sees the Documents group and this page. A user account with no linked employee record gets HTTP 400 and lands in the error state with 'No employee profile linked to this account'.
Session — any 401 from the API clears localStorage and hard-redirects to /login. Fifteen minutes with no mouse, key, click, scroll or touch event redirects to /login?timeout=1.
Responsive — 1 card per row below 640px, 2 from 640px, 3 from 1280px; the sidebar collapses to a hamburger-triggered overlay below 1024px; the header's 'FOne HR — …' caption is hidden below 640px.
mockData: Signed-in employee for all mock screens: Sneha Iyer, employee code FTN0042, role EMPLOYEE, Software Engineer in Engineering at Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd; header identity block shows 'Sneha Iyer' / 'EMPLOYEE · FTN0042' and the avatar reads 'SI'. Employee-code format is an alphabetic company prefix plus a zero-padded sequence, exactly as the seeded codes DEMO001–DEMO005 do it. Unread notification count on the bell: 3. Payroll cycle runs the 25th to the 24th, so a slip labelled 'August 2026' covers 25 Jul – 24 Aug 2026 (the page shows only the label, not the range). Nine cards, newest first: 'August 2026' Net Pay ₹61,480 | 'July 2026' Net Pay ₹61,480 | 'June 2026' Net Pay ₹58,265 (one loss-of-pay day) | 'May 2026' Net Pay ₹61,480 | 'April 2026' Net Pay ₹61,480 (revised CTC effective from the new financial year) | 'March 2026' Net Pay ₹52,310 | 'February 2026' Net Pay ₹52,310 | 'January 2026' Net Pay ₹52,310 | 'December 2025' with NO amount, so its sub-line reads 'Salary slip document'. Underlying components behind ₹61,480: Basic ₹32,000, HRA ₹12,800, Special Allowance ₹14,500, Conveyance ₹1,600, PF deduction ₹3,840, ESIC ₹0, TDS ₹2,150 — useful if a richer card is wanted, but the live screen prints only the net figure. Sample notification titles for the bell/drawer: 'Leave application approved' (body: 'Your Casual Leave for 03/08/2026 – 04/08/2026 has been approved by Arjun Mehta.'), 'Salary slip available' (body: 'Your salary slip for August 2026 is now available under Documents.'), 'Holiday announced' (body: 'Diwali on 08/11/2026 has been added to the holiday calendar.'), each timestamped like '18/09/2026 20:14:37'.

title: Offer Letter
purpose: Shows the employee their own employment offer letter, or all of them when the letter has been revised, so they can open or download the signed PDF.
layout: Same employee app shell as the salary-slips screen: 256px slate-900 sidebar on lg+ (Documents group expanded, 'Offer Letter' the active brand-600 pill), sticky white header with the 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' caption, bell and identity block, and a p-4 lg:p-8 body on a slate-100 background. PAGE BODY top-to-bottom: (1) PageHeader — h1 'Offer Letter' at text-2xl font-bold slate-800 with the subtitle 'Your employment offer letter(s)' at text-sm slate-500 directly beneath, margin-bottom 24px, no right-hand action slot. (2) A DELIBERATELY NARROW card grid: gap 16px, 1 column on mobile and 2 columns from the sm breakpoint (640px) and never more — and the whole grid is capped at max-width 768px (max-w-3xl) and left-aligned, so on a wide desktop the cards occupy only the left two-thirds of the content area with empty space to their right. This is the visual signature of the screen and must be preserved. Cards are NOT flex columns here (unlike the other two document screens), so with one long and one short title the two cards in a row can differ slightly in height. No table, no filters, no tabs.

widgets.label: Sidebar navigation (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Identical to the salary-slips screen: slate-900, 256px, F1HR light logo 30px tall at the top over a slate-800 divider; a 'COMPANY' 11px uppercase slate-500 caption above 'Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' in text-sm font-semibold slate-200; then the collapsible groups 'Home' (Home, Dashboard), 'Attendance & Leave' (Attendance, Leave Balance, Apply Leave, Leave History, plus Approvals only with leaves.approve), 'Documents' (Salary Slips, Offer Letter, Company Policies), an optional flat 'Payroll' link with documents.manage, an optional 'MANAGEMENT' section, and a flat 'Change Password' link; footer holds the red-on-hover 'Logout' button. Active child link is a solid brand-600 pill with white text — here that is 'Offer Letter', with its parent 'Documents' group auto-expanded and its ChevronDown rotated.

widgets.label: Top header bar (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Sticky white bar with bottom border slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8 py-3. Left: hamburger below lg, then 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' in text-sm slate-500 (hidden below 640px). Right: the Bell button with its red unread pill, the two-line identity block 'Sneha Iyer' / 'EMPLOYEE · FTN0042', and the 36px brand-600 circular avatar reading 'SI'.

widgets.label: Offer letter card grid
widgets.detail: Grid with gap 16px, grid-cols-1 then sm:grid-cols-2, wrapper capped at max-w-3xl (768px). One card per offer letter, ordered by upload time newest first — so a revised letter sits before the original. Each card is class 'card' (white, rounded-xl, 1px slate-200 border, small shadow) with p-5. CARD CONTENT, top to bottom: (1) A flex row with items-start and justify-between. Its LEFT element is a square icon tile, rounded-lg, padding 10px, background emerald-50, containing a lucide 'FileBadge' icon at 22px in emerald-600. Its RIGHT element is a status pill — see the badge widget. (2) The letter title in font-semibold slate-800 with margin-top 12px. The backend's default title format is literally 'Offer Letter - {EMPLOYEE_CODE}' and, for a revision, 'Offer Letter - {EMPLOYEE_CODE} (Revised)', so titles look like 'Offer Letter - FTN0042'. (3) A meta line in text-xs slate-400 with margin-top 4px reading the literal word 'Uploaded: ' followed by the upload date rendered DD/MM/YYYY (two-digit day, two-digit month, four-digit year, slash-separated; a missing date renders as an em dash '—'). (4) A button row: flex, gap 8px, margin-top 16px, TWO buttons each flex-1 so they split the card width in half, both class btn-secondary (white, 1px slate-300 border, slate-700 text, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium) — button 1 is an Eye icon at 15px plus the word 'View', button 2 is a Download icon at 15px plus the words 'Download PDF' (note the longer label than on the policies screen).

widgets.label: Original / Revised status pill
widgets.detail: One pill in the top-right corner of every offer-letter card, driven by the boolean is_revised. Shape for both: inline-flex, rounded-full, px-2.5 py-0.5, text-xs font-medium, no wrapping. When is_revised is TRUE the pill reads exactly 'Revised' in amber — bg-amber-100 with text-amber-700. When is_revised is FALSE the pill reads exactly 'Original' in green — bg-emerald-100 with text-emerald-700. There is no third state.

widgets.label: Info alert — no offer letter
widgets.detail: Rendered only when the employee has zero offer letters, as the FIRST CHILD OF THE GRID so it occupies one grid cell (roughly half the 768px wrapper on a wide screen) rather than the full width. Class: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-blue-50 / text-blue-700 / border-blue-200. Copy is exactly 'No offer letter uploaded yet. Please contact HR.'

widgets.label: Error alert — request failure
widgets.detail: Replaces the ENTIRE page (PageHeader included) on a failed list fetch or a failed View/Download. rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200, carrying the raw server message. Realistic strings: 'No employee profile linked to this account', 'Offer letter not found', 'Not allowed', 'File missing on server', 'Failed to fetch document'.

widgets.label: Loading spinner
widgets.detail: Shown in place of the whole page while the list is in flight: a centred 32px circle, rounded-full, 4px slate-200 border with a brand-600 top border, spinning, inside a flex container with py-16.

actions: View (Eye icon) — authenticated fetch of GET /api/documents/offer-letters/{id}/file, converted to a blob URL and opened in a NEW BROWSER TAB.
Download PDF (Download icon) — the same fetch, then a hidden anchor download named after the letter title with a .pdf extension, e.g. 'Offer Letter - FTN0042.pdf'.
Either failing swaps the whole page for the red error alert.
Sidebar group expand/collapse, navigation to any sibling route, 'Change Password', and 'Logout' (clears localStorage session and redirects to /login).

Header: hamburger opens the mobile sidebar overlay; the bell opens the notification dropdown; 'Mark all as read'; clicking a notification opens the reader drawer with that card expanded; 'View all notifications'; 'Open' inside an expanded notification navigates to its link.

NO destructive actions and no upload control for the employee — uploading, retitling, marking as revised and deleting an offer letter all require the documents.manage permission and live on the admin Documents screen.
states: Loading — the whole page is just the centred spinner; the PageHeader is not rendered.
Loaded, single letter — one card in the left grid cell, right cell empty, whole grid capped at 768px.
Loaded, revised — two or more cards; the newest (the revision, amber 'Revised' pill) appears first, the original (green 'Original' pill) after it.
Empty — PageHeader plus the blue info alert 'No offer letter uploaded yet. Please contact HR.' in the first grid cell.
Error — the whole page is just the red alert; no retry, no dismiss.

Permission — every non-admin user can reach this route. An employee is served only their own letters; a direct hit on another employee's file returns 403 'Not allowed' unless the caller has documents.manage (in which case the API returns every employee's letters joined with emp_code and employee_name — but this employee-facing page never renders those extra columns).
Session — a 401 clears the session and redirects to /login; fifteen idle minutes redirect to /login?timeout=1.
Responsive — 1 card per row below 640px, 2 above; the 768px cap means the grid never grows past two columns no matter how wide the window; sidebar becomes an overlay below 1024px.

Two cards, newest first. CARD 1: title 'Offer Letter - FTN0042 (Revised)', amber 'Revised' pill, meta line 'Uploaded: 12/04/2026' — this is the appraisal-cycle revision that lifted the annual CTC from ₹7,80,000 to ₹9,20,000 effective 01/04/2026. title: Company Policies
purpose: A browsable library of the company's official policy PDFs, grouped visually by category, that any employee can read or download.
layout: Same employee app shell: 256px slate-900 sidebar on lg+ (Documents group expanded, 'Company Policies' the active brand-600 pill), sticky white header, p-4 lg:p-8 body on slate-100. PAGE BODY top-to-bottom: (1) PageHeader — h1 'Company Policies' at text-2xl font-bold slate-800 with the subtitle 'Official company policy documents' at text-sm slate-500 beneath it, margin-bottom 24px, no right-hand action slot (no search box, no category filter, no upload button — the employee view is read-only and unfiltered). (2) A full-width responsive card grid: gap 16px, 1 column on mobile, 2 columns from 640px, 3 columns from 1280px, NOT capped in width (unlike the offer-letter screen). Cards are flex columns and the description block is the flex-grow element, which is what makes every card in a row end up exactly the same height with its date line and buttons aligned along the bottom edge regardless of how long the description is. Policies are ordered ALPHABETICALLY BY TITLE ascending, not by date and not grouped by category — categories appear only as coloured pills scattered through the grid. No table, no tabs, no modals on this screen.

widgets.label: Sidebar navigation (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Identical to the other two document screens: slate-900, 256px, F1HR light logo 30px at the top, a 'COMPANY' caption over 'Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd', the collapsible groups 'Home' (Home, Dashboard), 'Attendance & Leave' (Attendance, Leave Balance, Apply Leave, Leave History, plus Approvals with leaves.approve), 'Documents' (Salary Slips, Offer Letter, Company Policies), an optional flat 'Payroll' link, an optional 'MANAGEMENT' section, a flat 'Change Password' link, and a 'Logout' footer button that turns red on hover. Here the active brand-600 pill is 'Company Policies' inside the expanded 'Documents' group.

widgets.label: Top header bar (shared employee shell)
widgets.detail: Sticky white bar, bottom border slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8 py-3. Left: hamburger below 1024px, then 'FOne HR — Futurn Technologies Pvt Ltd' in text-sm slate-500, hidden below 640px. Right: Bell with red unread pill, identity block 'Sneha Iyer' over 'EMPLOYEE · FTN0042', and the 36px brand-600 avatar circle reading 'SI'.

widgets.label: Policy card grid
widgets.detail: Grid, gap 16px, grid-cols-1 / sm:grid-cols-2 / xl:grid-cols-3, full content width. One card per policy, sorted A–Z by title. Each card is class 'card' (white, rounded-xl, 1px slate-200 border, small shadow), p-5, display flex, flex-direction column. CARD CONTENT, top to bottom: (1) A flex row with items-start and justify-between: LEFT is a square icon tile, rounded-lg, padding 10px, background purple-50, holding a lucide 'BookOpen' icon at 22px in purple-600; RIGHT is the category pill (see the badge widget). (2) The policy title in font-semibold slate-800, margin-top 12px. (3) The description in text-sm slate-500, margin-top 4px, and crucially flex-1 — it absorbs the leftover vertical space, so short descriptions push nothing and long ones set the row height. Descriptions are NOT truncated or clamped on this employee page (the admin table truncates them at 300px; this one does not). (4) A meta line in text-xs slate-400, margin-top 8px, reading the literal word 'Updated: ' followed by the upload date rendered DD/MM/YYYY (a missing date renders as an em dash '—'). (5) A button row: flex, gap 8px, margin-top 16px, TWO flex-1 buttons of class btn-secondary (white, 1px slate-300 border, slate-700 text, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium, hover bg-slate-50) — button 1 is an Eye icon at 15px plus the word 'View', button 2 is a Download icon at 15px plus the single word 'Download' (shorter than the offer-letter screen's 'Download PDF').

widgets.label: Category pill
widgets.detail: One pill per card, top-right, printing the policy's free-text category verbatim. It is ALWAYS purple regardless of the category value — inline-flex, rounded-full, px-2.5 py-0.5, text-xs font-medium, bg-purple-100 with text-purple-700, whitespace-nowrap. Category is an unconstrained text field on the admin upload form (its placeholder suggests 'e.g. HR, Leave, IT'), so real values are short single words or short phrases such as HR, Leave, IT, Finance, Compliance, Security.

widgets.label: Error alert — request failure
widgets.detail: Replaces the ENTIRE page including the PageHeader on a failed list fetch or a failed View/Download. rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200, showing the raw server message. Realistic strings: 'Policy not found', 'File missing on server', 'Failed to fetch document', 'Request failed'.

widgets.label: Loading spinner
widgets.detail: Shown in place of the whole page while the policy list is loading: a centred 32px circle, rounded-full, 4px slate-200 border with a brand-600 top border, spinning, inside a flex container with py-16.

widgets.label: Empty grid (no empty-state copy)
widgets.detail: IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE from the other two document screens: this page has NO empty-state alert. When the company has uploaded zero policies the PageHeader still renders and the grid below it is simply blank — no 'No policies' message, no illustration, no call to action. Reproduce that bare gap faithfully if an empty variant is mocked.

actions: View (Eye icon) — authenticated fetch of GET /api/documents/policies/{id}/file, converted to a blob URL and opened in a NEW BROWSER TAB; the server also writes a POLICY_DOWNLOADED audit entry.

Sidebar group expand/collapse, navigation to any sibling route, 'Change Password', and 'Logout' (clears localStorage and redirects to /login).

Header: hamburger opens the mobile sidebar overlay; the bell opens the notification dropdown; 'Mark all as read'; clicking a notification opens the reader drawer with that card expanded; 'View all notifications'; 'Open' inside an expanded notification navigates to its link.

NO destructive or authoring actions on this employee view — the Upload Policy button, the Replace (RefreshCw) action and the Delete (Trash2) action all live on the admin Documents screen behind documents.manage and must NOT appear here.

Permission — the policy list is company-wide and ungated for reading: every authenticated tenant user sees every policy. Only uploading, replacing and deleting require documents.manage.
