title: Employee Management
purpose: The HR master list of employee records — search, add, edit, upload a photo, reset a password, lock/unlock or enable/disable the login, end probation early, and delete an employee together with all of their records.
layout: Same app shell as /admin (fixed 256px slate-900 sidebar, sticky white topbar, main p-4 lg:p-8 on a slate-100 background), with 'Employees' as the highlighted bg-brand-600 sidebar link. Main column, top to bottom: (1) PageHeader — flex-wrap justify-between mb-6: left is the 2xl bold slate-800 heading 'Employee Management' over a text-sm slate-500 subtitle 'Add, edit, search and manage employee accounts'; right is a single primary button '+ Add Employee' (lucide Plus at 16px then the label, bg-brand-600 white, rounded-lg px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium). (2) An alert slot, mb-4, that shows a red Alert on error and a green Alert on success — only one at a time, and only when there is a message. (3) A search card: white card p-4 mb-4 containing a relative max-w-md wrapper with a 16px lucide Search icon absolutely positioned left-3 and vertically centred in slate-400, and an input with extra left padding (!pl-9), placeholder 'Search by name, code, email or department…'. (4) The employee table, wrapped in a horizontally drag-scrollable white card (overflow-x-auto, cursor-grab, cursor-grabbing while dragging): a min-w-full table with divide-y divide-slate-200, a bg-slate-50 thead whose cells are px-4 py-3 text-left text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider slate-500, and a tbody with divide-y divide-slate-100 whose cells are px-4 py-3 text-sm. The first two columns are frozen: 'Code' is sticky at left:0 with a hard width of exactly 112px (min and max both 112px), and 'Name' is sticky at left:112px; the frozen header cells sit on bg-slate-50 (z-20), the frozen body cells on bg-white and switch to bg-slate-50 on row hover so they track the row; once the table is scrolled sideways the Name column gains a right-edge shadow (box-shadow 6px 0 8px -6px rgba(15,23,42,0.25)). Rows hover to bg-slate-50. (5) Three dialogs rendered above everything when open — Add/Edit Employee (wide), Reset Password, Upload Employee Photo. All modals are centred, p-4 viewport padding, with a slate-900/50 backdrop that closes on click, the panel itself a white card, max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto p-6, a header row with the text-lg font-bold slate-800 title on the left and a 2xl slate-400 '×' close button on the right, mb-4.

widgets.label: Search box
widgets.detail: Single text input, full width of a max-w-md wrapper inside its own white card (p-4, mb-4). Left-inset 16px Search icon (slate-400). Placeholder: 'Search by name, code, email or department…'. No dropdown filters, no status toggle, no sort control, no pagination anywhere on this screen. Typing is debounced 250ms before the list reloads; the server matches the term case-insensitively against employee code, first name, last name, email and department name, and always returns rows ordered by employee code ascending.

widgets.label: Employee list
widgets.detail: Exactly 8 columns, in this rendered order: 1) 'Code' — frozen, 112px, value in font-semibold. 2) 'Name' — frozen at 112px offset; cell is a flex row gap-3: a 36px (h-9 w-9) round avatar (either the uploaded photo, object-cover inside a bg-slate-100 circle with a slate-200 border, or a fallback circle bg-brand-100 text-brand-700 text-xs font-bold showing the first letter of the first name plus the first letter of the last name), then a two-line block — line 1 font-medium slate-800 full name, followed inline by a purple badge with the user's ROLE NAME whenever the role is set and is not 'EMPLOYEE' (e.g. DIRECTOR, HR, OWNER, or a custom role name); line 2 text-xs slate-500 email. 3) 'Department' — plain text, or an em dash '—' when unset. 4) 'Designation' — plain text or '—'. 5) 'Manager' — the reporting manager's full name or '—'. 6) 'Status' — a badge, green for 'Active' and red for 'Inactive'; when the employee's probation_until is today or later a second line appears beneath it (mt-1, flex gap-1.5) with an amber badge reading 'Probation → DD/MM/YYYY' next to a tiny 10px font-bold brand-600 text button 'Remove' (hover underline, tooltip 'End probation period immediately'). 7) 'Login' — a single badge: red 'Locked' if the account is locked, else green 'Enabled' if active, else slate 'Disabled'. 8) 'Actions' — header is right-aligned ('text-right'); cell is a right-aligned flex row of six 16px icon buttons with gap-1.5, each p-1.5 rounded with hover:bg-slate-200. The table is wider than the viewport by design: it can be dragged sideways by grabbing any non-interactive part of it (mouse only; presses that land on a button, link, input, select, textarea or label are left alone, and a drag of more than 3px suppresses the click it would otherwise have fired).

widgets.label: Per-row action icons (Actions column, left to right)
widgets.detail: 1) Upload Photo — lucide Image, slate-600, tooltip 'Upload Photo', opens the photo modal. 2) Edit — lucide Pencil, slate-600, tooltip 'Edit', opens the Edit Employee modal prefilled. 3) Reset password — lucide KeyRound, slate-600, tooltip 'Reset password', opens the Reset Password modal. 4) Lock/Unlock — when the account is unlocked: lucide Lock in amber-600, tooltip 'Lock account'; when locked: lucide Unlock in emerald-600, tooltip 'Unlock account'. Fires immediately with no confirmation. 5) Power — lucide Power, slate-600 with tooltip 'Disable login' when the account is active, emerald-600 with tooltip 'Enable login' when it is not. Fires immediately with no confirmation. 6) Delete — lucide Trash2 in red-600 with hover:bg-red-100, tooltip 'Delete employee'; opens a native confirm before acting.

widgets.label: Add Employee / Edit Employee
widgets.detail: Wide dialog (max-w-3xl). Title is 'Add Employee' in add mode and 'Edit Employee' in edit mode. Body is one form laid out as grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-4; every field has a .label above it (block text-xs font-semibold slate-600 uppercase tracking-wide mb-1) and a .input control (w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm, brand-500 focus ring). Fields in exact source order: (1) 'Employee Code' — text input, placeholder 'EMP011', required, DISABLED (greyed) in edit mode. (2) 'Status' — select with exactly two options, 'Active' and 'Inactive'; defaults to Active. (3) 'First Name' — text, required. (4) 'Last Name' — text, required. (5) 'Email' — type=email, required; server rejects an address already registered anywhere on the platform with 'That email is already registered on the platform'. (6) 'Phone' — text, optional. (7) 'Emergency Contact (optional)' — text, placeholder 'e.g. 9876543210'. (8) 'Date of Joining' — custom DatePicker, required. (9) 'Date of Birth (must be 18+)' — custom DatePicker, required, with a hard max of today-minus-18-years; dates after that max are greyed out and unclickable, and the server also rejects anyone under 18 with 'Employee must be at least 18 years old'. (10) 'Department' — select whose first option is 'None / Select department' followed by the department names. (11) 'Designation' — select whose first option is 'None / Select designation' followed by the designation titles. (12) 'Reporting Manager' — select whose first option is '—' (or 'No employees yet' when no active employees exist); the other options are every active employee except the one being edited, each labelled '<CODE> — <Full Name>' e.g. 'FTRN007 — Arjun Mehta'. Helper line below in text-xs slate-400: 'Any employee can be a manager — add the manager as an employee first, then select them here.' (13) 'Probation Until (optional)' — a flex row: the DatePicker takes the remaining width and, only when a date is set, a secondary 'Clear' button (white, slate-300 border, tooltip 'Remove probation') sits beside it. Helper line: 'While on probation: unpaid leave only, leave balance locked (no accrual, no deduction).' In ADD mode only, choosing a Date of Joining auto-fills this field with DOJ + the company's default probation months (read from org settings) when it is still blank and that default is greater than zero. (14) 'PAN Number (optional)' — text. (15) 'Bank Name (optional)' — text. (16) 'Bank Account No. (optional)' — text. (17) 'Bank IFSC (optional)' — text. (18) 'User Role' — select whose first option is 'EMPLOYEE (default)'; the other options are the role names, with ' (custom)' appended to any non-system role, e.g. 'OWNER', 'DIRECTOR', 'HR', 'Payroll Admin (custom)'. Helper line: 'HR and DIRECTOR can approve leave. Custom roles are defined by the admin in Roles & Access.' (19) ADD MODE ONLY, spanning both columns, text-xs slate-500: 'A login account is created automatically (username = employee code) with a randomly generated temporary password, which is emailed to the employee. They are required to change it at first login.' (20) Footer spanning both columns, flex justify-end gap-2 pt-2: secondary 'Cancel' and primary submit 'Save Employee', which becomes 'Saving…' and is disabled while the request is in flight. Required fields per the server: employee code, first name, last name, email, date of joining, date of birth.

widgets.label: DatePicker control (used by Date of Joining, Date of Birth, Probation Until)
widgets.detail: Not a native date input. A text box showing the date as DD/MM/YYYY with placeholder 'Select Date' and a 16px lucide Calendar button inset at the right edge (slate-400, hover slate-600). Typing auto-inserts the slashes as digits are entered and only commits a value once all 10 characters form a real date between 1900 and 2100 and inside any min/max. Focusing the box or clicking the calendar icon opens a 288px-wide (w-72) popover below it: white, border-slate-200, rounded-xl, shadow-xl, p-3. Popover header: a ChevronLeft previous-month button, a month select (January…December) beside a year select spanning current year minus 80 to current year plus 10, and a ChevronRight next-month button. Then a 7-column weekday strip in 11px bold slate-500 reading Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa, then a 6x7 (42-cell) grid of 32px rounded-lg day buttons: days from the neighbouring months render in slate-300, the selected day is bg-brand-600 white, out-of-range days are slate-200 and not clickable, others hover bg-slate-100. When the field is optional and already has a value, a bordered footer row shows an 11px bold red 'Clear Date' link on the right. Clicking anywhere outside closes the popover.

widgets.label: Reset Password
widgets.detail: Narrow dialog (max-w-lg), title 'Reset Password'. Body space-y-4: (1) a text-sm slate-600 sentence 'Set a new password for Full Name (EMPCODE).'; (2) a red Alert slot shown on validation or server error; (3) field 'New password' — a plain text input (the value is deliberately visible, not masked), placeholder 'At least 8 characters', autocomplete off, autofocused; (4) a text-xs slate-500 helper paragraph: 'The new password is emailed to the employee automatically. It is shown here in plain text as well, so you can pass it on if the email does not arrive — you will be told either way. Common defaults such as Welcome@123 are rejected. The employee must change it at first login, and any account lockout is cleared.' — with 'Welcome@123' rendered in a monospace style; (5) footer flex justify-end gap-2 pt-1: secondary 'Cancel' and primary submit 'Reset Password', which becomes 'Resetting…' and is disabled while submitting. Validation: the client refuses anything shorter than 8 characters with the inline error 'Password must be at least 8 characters.'; the server additionally rejects a handful of common defaults (Welcome@123, Admin@123, password, Password1, 12345678, changeme) with 'That password is too common — please choose another' and anything longer than 200 characters.

widgets.label: Upload Employee Photo
widgets.detail: Narrow dialog (max-w-lg), title 'Upload Employee Photo'. Body space-y-4: (1) text-sm slate-600 sentence 'Upload a profile photo for Full Name.'; (2) a red Alert slot for upload errors; (3) field 'Photo File' — an input of type=file styled with the .input class, required, accepting image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp and image/heic only; (4) footer flex justify-end gap-2 pt-1: secondary 'Cancel' and primary submit 'Upload Photo', which becomes 'Uploading…' and is disabled while uploading. Closing via Cancel or the × also clears any error.

widgets.label: Row badges
widgets.detail: All use the shared pill style (rounded-full px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium). Status column: 'Active' green (emerald-100/700), 'Inactive' red (red-100/700). Probation: amber (amber-100/700) reading 'Probation → DD/MM/YYYY'. Login column: 'Locked' red, 'Enabled' green, 'Disabled' slate (slate-100/600). Role chip next to the name: purple (purple-100/700), carrying the raw role name in the casing the system stores it (DIRECTOR, HR, OWNER) or the custom role's own name.

widgets.label: Native confirm dialogs (browser confirm, not styled)
widgets.detail: Delete: 'Delete FTRN009 (Sneha Iyer) and all their records? This cannot be undone.' — deleting removes the employee's attendance, leave applications, leave balances, leave ledger, salary slips, offer letters and login account, and clears them as anyone else's reporting manager. End probation: 'Confirm ending probation for Nikhil Bansal?'. Lock, unlock, enable and disable are NOT confirmed — they take effect on the first click.

widgets.label: Inline result messages
widgets.detail: A single alert region directly under the page header. Success is a green Alert (emerald-50 bg, emerald-200 border, emerald-700 text) that auto-clears after 4 seconds; error is a red Alert that stays until the next action. Messages are the server's own wording, for example: 'Employee created — credentials emailed to nikhil.bansal@futurn.in'; 'Employee created, but the welcome email could NOT be delivered (SMTP timeout). Set a password for them from the Reset Password button and hand it over directly.'; 'Employee updated'; 'Employee deleted'; 'Account locked for FTRN012'; 'Account unlocked for FTRN012'; 'Account disabled for FTRN021'; 'Account enabled for FTRN021'; 'Password reset for FTRN018 — emailed to deepa.krishnan@futurn.in'; 'Probation ended for Nikhil Bansal'; 'Photo uploaded successfully'.

actions: '+ Add Employee' (primary, page header) → opens the wide Add Employee modal with a blank form (Status pre-set to 'Active').
Search input → debounced 250ms, refetches the list; clearing it restores the full list.
Drag anywhere on the table body → scrolls the table sideways while the Code and Name columns stay pinned; a drag that moves more than 3px swallows the click so no row button fires.
Row 'Upload Photo' icon → opens the Upload Employee Photo modal for that employee.
Row 'Edit' icon → opens the Edit Employee modal prefilled with the row, Employee Code disabled.
Row 'Reset password' icon → opens the Reset Password modal naming that employee.
Row 'Lock account' / 'Unlock account' icon → immediate POST, no confirmation; unlocking also clears an automatic failed-attempt lockout. Shows a success alert and reloads the list.
Row 'Disable login' / 'Enable login' Power icon → immediate POST, no confirmation. Shows a success alert and reloads the list.

Row 'Delete employee' icon (DESTRUCTIVE) → native confirm 'Delete <CODE> (<Name>) and all their records? This cannot be undone.'; on OK it permanently removes the employee and all their attendance, leave, balance, ledger, salary-slip, offer-letter and login rows.
'Remove' text button beside a Probation badge (DESTRUCTIVE-ish) → native confirm 'Confirm ending probation for <First> <Last>?'; on OK it clears probation immediately.

Add/Edit modal: 'Save Employee' submits (label flips to 'Saving…'); 'Cancel' or the × closes without saving. On add, the server creates the login account, generates a random temporary password and emails the credentials with the Employee Manual PDF attached.
Add/Edit modal: 'Clear' button next to Probation Until wipes that date.

Reset Password modal: 'Reset Password' submits (label flips to 'Resetting…'); on a delivery failure the modal STAYS OPEN and shows the warning in the error alert so HR still has the typed password on screen; 'Cancel' or × closes.
Upload Photo modal: 'Upload Photo' submits the chosen file (label flips to 'Uploading…'); 'Cancel' or × closes and clears the error.
Clicking a modal's dark backdrop closes that modal.
states: Loading (initial and on every search): the table area is replaced by the centred 32px brand-600 spinner inside a py-16 block. The page header, alert slot and search card remain visible.
Empty search result: a single table row spanning all 8 columns, centred, text-slate-500, py-10, reading 'No employees found.'
Error: a red Alert under the page header carrying the server message; the previously loaded table stays on screen.
Success: a green Alert under the page header that disappears by itself after 4 seconds.

Conditional row content — probation: the amber 'Probation → DD/MM/YYYY' badge and its 'Remove' button render only when the employee has a probation_until date that is today or in the future; past probation dates render nothing.
Conditional row content — role chip: the purple role badge renders only when the linked login has a role that is not 'EMPLOYEE'.
Conditional row content — avatar: a real photo renders when one has been uploaded (fetched with the auth token and swapped in as a blob), otherwise the brand-100 initials circle.
Conditional cells: Department, Designation and Manager each fall back to an em dash '—' when unset.
Conditional Login badge: Locked (red) wins over Enabled/Disabled; otherwise Enabled (green) when the account is active and Disabled (slate) when it is not.
Modal mode differences: in Edit mode the Employee Code input is disabled and the 'A login account is created automatically…' note is absent; in Add mode the code is editable and the note is shown.

Drag affordance: the table only shows the grab cursor when it is actually wider than its container, and the frozen Name column only gets its right-edge shadow once the table has been scrolled away from the left.
Permission denied: a user without employees.view never sees this page in the nav and the API answers 403; the mutating buttons require employees.manage.
Session expiry: any 401 clears the session and hard-redirects to /login.

title: Apply Leave
purpose: Lets any logged-in employee submit a new leave request, with an optional supporting document, for HR/Director approval.
layout: Single column page. (1) PageHeader block at top: h1 'Apply Leave' (text-2xl bold slate-800) with subtitle 'Submit a new leave request for approval' (text-sm slate-500) directly beneath; no header action buttons on this page; mb-6. (2) Below it a CSS grid: 1 column on mobile, 3 columns at lg breakpoint, gap-6. LEFT: a white card (rounded-xl, border slate-200, shadow-sm, p-6) spanning 2 of the 3 columns — it contains, top to bottom, the conditional probation info alert, the conditional error alert, the conditional success alert, then the leave form (vertical stack, space-y-4). RIGHT: a second white card (p-6, height fits content, does NOT stretch) containing the 'How approval works' numbered vertical timeline. Global design tokens: brand-50 #f0f6ff, brand-100 #dcebfe, brand-500 #2563eb, brand-600 #1d4ed8, brand-700 #1e40af, brand-900 #1e293b; .card = bg-white rounded-xl border-slate-200 shadow-sm; .input = w-full rounded-lg border-slate-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus ring brand-500; .label = block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600 UPPERCASE tracking-wide mb-1; .btn-primary = bg-brand-600 text-white rounded-lg px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium.

widgets.label: Probation info alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: Full-width alert bar, rounded-lg, border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-blue-50 / text-blue-700 / border-blue-200. Exact copy: 'You are on probation until 31/12/2026. Leave you take is unpaid — your leave balance is locked and will not be affected.' The fragments 'probation until 31/12/2026' and 'unpaid' are bold. Rendered inside a mb-4 wrapper, above the form. Only shown when the employee is on probation.

widgets.label: Error alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: Same alert shape, bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200. Shows the raw API error string. Real messages from the backend: 'During probationary periods, you can only apply for unpaid leaves.', 'Insufficient balance: 3.00 day(s) available, 5 requested', 'You already have a pending/approved leave overlapping those dates (#42: 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-15)', 'Selected range has no working days', 'To date cannot be before from date', 'Leave type, dates and reason are required', 'No leave balance found for this type'.

widgets.label: Success alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: Same alert shape, bg-emerald-50 / text-emerald-700 / border-emerald-200. Exact composed copy: 'Leave application submitted (2 working days). HR and the Director have been notified. Redirecting…' — the leading sentence is the server message ('Leave application submitted', or 'Leave application submitted as UNPAID (your balance is not affected)' when unpaid), followed by '(N working day/days)'; 'day' is singular when days is 1.

widgets.label: Apply Leave form
widgets.detail: Vertical stack, space-y-4. FIELD 1 — 'LEAVE TYPE' (label style: uppercase text-xs semibold slate-600): a <select> with class .input, required. First option is the placeholder 'Select leave type…' with empty value. Then one option per leave type, in id order: 'Casual Leave', 'Earned Leave', 'Sick Leave', 'Comp Off', 'Unpaid Leave'. When the employee is on probation every option whose code is not 'UL' is disabled and its text has the suffix ' — (Disabled during probation)', and 'Unpaid Leave' is auto-selected on load. FIELD 2 — 'Single Day Leave' checkbox (see its own widget). FIELD 3 — dates (see date widgets). FIELD 4 — 'REASON': <textarea> class .input, rows=3, required, placeholder 'Reason for leave…'. FIELD 5 — 'SUPPORTING DOCUMENT (OPTIONAL)': see the upload widget. Finally the submit button. Client-side validation is HTML required-attributes only; the day count and balance checks happen server-side.

widgets.label: Leave-type helper line (three mutually exclusive variants)
widgets.detail: A single line of text-xs directly under the Leave Type select, mt-1. Variant A (selected type code = UL): text-brand-600 font-medium — 'Unpaid Leave — no balance is required or deducted.' Variant B (selected type is not UL and employee is NOT on probation): text-slate-500 — 'Balance: 7.50 day(s) (accrues 1.5/month)' where the number 7.50 is font-semibold text-brand-700 and is the balance to 2 decimal places. Variant C (employee IS on probation, always shown regardless of selection): text-amber-600 font-semibold — '⚠️ You are on probation. During probationary periods, an employee can only take unpaid leaves.'

widgets.label: Single Day Leave toggle
widgets.detail: A flex row, items-center, gap-2. An <input type=checkbox> id='single-day', h-4 w-4, rounded, border-slate-300, accent/text brand-600, focus ring brand-500, cursor-pointer. Next to it a <label for='single-day'> reading 'Single Day Leave' in text-xs font-semibold text-slate-700, cursor-pointer, select-none. Unchecked by default. Checking it collapses the two-date row into a single 'Date' field and copies the current From Date into To Date.

widgets.label: Date field — single-day mode
widgets.detail: Shown only when the Single Day Leave checkbox is ticked. One field, full width, label 'DATE', using the custom DatePicker component with placeholder 'Select Date', required. Selecting a date sets both from_date and to_date to the same value.

widgets.label: Date fields — range mode (default)
widgets.detail: Shown when the checkbox is unticked. A grid: 1 column on mobile, 2 columns at sm, gap-4. Left field label 'FROM DATE', custom DatePicker, placeholder 'Select Date', required — if the existing To Date is earlier than the new From Date, To Date is silently pushed forward to match. Right field label 'TO DATE', custom DatePicker, placeholder 'Select Date', required, with min set to the From Date so earlier days are greyed out and unclickable.

widgets.label: DatePicker popover (custom component, used by both date fields)
widgets.detail: Closed state: a text input (not a native date input) with class .input plus bg-white, border-slate-300, rounded-lg, pl-3 pr-10 py-2, text-sm text-slate-800, hover:border-brand-400, focus:border-brand-500. It displays the date as DD/MM/YYYY and accepts typing — digits are auto-masked with slashes as you type (2 digits, slash, 2 digits, slash, 4 digits). A calendar icon button (lucide Calendar, 16px, slate-400, hover slate-600) sits absolutely at right-3, vertically centred, and toggles the popover. Open state: an absolutely positioned white panel, left-0, mt-1.5, w-72, border-slate-200, rounded-xl, shadow-xl, z-50, p-3, select-none. Panel header is a flex row: a ChevronLeft button (16px, p-1, rounded-lg, hover bg-slate-100) on the left; in the centre two small borderless <select> dropdowns side by side in text-xs font-bold text-slate-700 — the month select listing January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December, and the year select listing every year from (current year − 80) to (current year + 10), i.e. 1946 through 2036; a ChevronRight button on the right. Below the header a 7-column row of weekday initials in text-[11px] font-bold text-slate-500: Su, Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa. Below that a fixed 42-cell 7-column grid, gap-1, text-xs: each day is an 8×8 rounded-lg button; days belonging to the previous/next month are text-slate-300; the selected day is bg-brand-600 with white semibold text; hoverable days get hover:bg-slate-100; days outside the min/max range are text-slate-200 with cursor-not-allowed. If a value is set AND the field is not required, a footer strip appears (mt-2, pt-2, border-t slate-100, right-aligned) with a 'Clear Date' link in text-[11px] font-bold text-red-500. Clicking anywhere outside closes the popover.

widgets.label: Supporting Document (optional)
widgets.detail: Label 'SUPPORTING DOCUMENT (OPTIONAL)'. The control is a clickable <label> styled as a dropzone: flex row, items-center, gap-3, rounded-lg, border-2 border-dashed border-slate-300, p-4, cursor-pointer, hover:border-brand-400. Inside: a lucide Paperclip icon at 18px in slate-400, then text-sm slate-600 reading 'Click to attach a file (e.g. medical certificate) — PDF or image, max 10 MB'. Once a file is chosen that sentence is replaced by the file name in font-medium text-brand-700, e.g. 'apollo-medical-certificate.pdf'. The real <input type=file> is visually hidden; accept='.pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.doc,.docx'; server enforces 10 MB max and exactly 1 file. Beneath the dropzone, a text-xs text-slate-400 note, mt-1: 'Weekends and company holidays are excluded automatically from the day count.'

widgets.label: Submit button
widgets.detail: A single .btn-primary button (bg-brand-600, white text, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium, hover bg-brand-700), left-aligned at the bottom of the form. Label 'Submit Request'. While submitting the label becomes 'Submitting…' and the button is disabled (opacity-50, cursor-not-allowed).

widgets.label: How approval works (right-hand card)
widgets.detail: Card p-6. Heading h3 'How approval works' in font-bold text-slate-800, mb-4. Below it an ordered list rendered as a vertical timeline: a 2px left border in brand-200, ml-3, space-y-6 between items, each item ml-5. Each step has a 5×5 circular numbered marker positioned at -left-[11px] with text-[10px] font-bold — step 1's marker is filled bg-brand-600 with white text, steps 2–4 are bg-white with a 2px brand-300 border and brand-600 text. The four steps, in order, verbatim: 1. 'You submit the request' 2. 'HR and the Director are emailed' 3. 'Any ONE of them approves or rejects' 4. 'You and your manager are notified'. Each step label is text-sm font-medium text-slate-700. Footer paragraph, mt-5, text-xs text-slate-500: 'A single approval from HR or the Director fully approves the leave. Your reporting manager receives an intimation only.'

actions: Submit Request — posts the form as multipart/form-data to POST /api/leaves/apply (fields: leave_type_id, from_date, to_date, reason, optional document). On success shows the green alert and auto-redirects to /leave/history after 1.8 seconds. On failure shows the red alert and re-enables the button.
Tick 'Single Day Leave' — swaps the From/To date pair for a single 'Date' field and copies the already-chosen From Date into To Date.
Calendar icon button — opens/closes the DatePicker popover. Clicking outside closes it.
DatePicker prev-month / next-month chevrons — step the visible month, rolling the year at the boundaries.
DatePicker month and year dropdowns — jump the calendar to any month between 1946 and 2036.
DatePicker day cell — selects the date, writes it back as DD/MM/YYYY, and closes the popover. Disabled for days before the From Date on the To Date field.
'Clear Date' link — wipes the field (only rendered on non-required date fields, so it does not appear on this screen's fields).
Click the dashed document dropzone — opens the OS file chooser, limited to .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .doc, .docx.
Select a leave type — re-renders the helper line beneath the select (balance, unpaid notice, or probation warning).
states: Default: no alerts; Leave Type on the 'Select leave type…' placeholder; range-mode date fields empty; submit button enabled.

Loading data: the leave-type and balance fetches happen on mount and fail silently — if they error the select shows only the placeholder option and no helper line ever appears. There is no skeleton or spinner on this page.
Submitting: button disabled, label 'Submitting…'.
Success: green alert, then redirect to /leave/history after 1.8s. The button stays disabled through the redirect.
Error: red alert above the form, button re-enabled, form values preserved.

On probation: blue info alert at the top; 'Unpaid Leave' force-selected on load; every other leave type option disabled and suffixed ' — (Disabled during probation)'; the amber '⚠️ You are on probation…' line always shown under the select; balance line suppressed.
Unpaid Leave selected (not on probation): the brand-coloured 'Unpaid Leave — no balance is required or deducted.' line replaces the balance line.
Single-day mode: two date fields collapse to one.
No permission gate — every authenticated employee can reach this route; there is no permission-denied state.
mockData: Logged-in user: Ananya Deshpande (EMP014), Senior Software Engineer, Engineering, reporting to Vikram Rao (EMP006). Leave types with their monthly accrual rates exactly as configured: Casual Leave (CL) 1/month, Earned Leave (EL) 1.5/month, Sick Leave (SL) 0.75/month, Comp Off (CO) 0/month, Unpaid Leave (UL) 0/month. Filled-in example: Leave Type = 'Earned Leave'; helper line 'Balance: 7.50 day(s) (accrues 1.5/month)'; Single Day Leave unticked; From Date 05/10/2026, To Date 07/10/2026; Reason 'Attending my sister's wedding in Nashik.'; attached file 'apollo-medical-certificate.pdf'. Success alert to show: 'Leave application submitted (3 working days). HR and the Director have been notified. Redirecting…'. Probation-variant example: Nikhil Bhatt (EMP031), joined 01/08/2026, alert reads 'You are on probation until 31/01/2027. Leave you take is unpaid — your leave balance is locked and will not be affected.' Note: this screen displays no currency at all — do not invent salary or INR fields here.

title: Leave Balance
purpose: Shows the logged-in employee their per-type leave balances and the full credit/deduction ledger that produced them.
layout: Single column, three stacked blocks. (1) PageHeader: flex row, wrap, items-center, justify-between, gap-3, mb-6 — left side h1 'Leave Balance' (text-2xl bold slate-800) with subtitle 'Balances accrue monthly and carry over — decimals included' (text-sm slate-500); right side a single .btn-primary link labelled 'Apply Leave'. (2) Optional probation info alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (3) Stat-card grid: 1 column on mobile, 2 at sm, 4 at xl, gap-4, mb-6 — one card per leave type. (4) A .card with horizontal overflow containing the balance summary table, mb-6. (5) A final .card with horizontal overflow containing a small heading block (px-4 pt-4 pb-1) and then the ledger table (mt-2).

widgets.label: Header action
widgets.detail: One .btn-primary anchor, text 'Apply Leave', links to /leave/apply. Sits on the right of the PageHeader row.

widgets.label: Probation info alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: bg-blue-50 / text-blue-700 / border-blue-200, rounded-lg, px-4 py-3, text-sm, in a mb-4 wrapper. Exact copy: 'You are on probation until 31/01/2027. Your leave balance is locked — nothing accrues and nothing is deducted; any leave you take is unpaid.' The fragments 'probation until 31/01/2027' and 'locked' are bold.

widgets.label: Per-leave-type balance card (one per type, 4 across at xl)
widgets.detail: A .card with p-5. Line 1: the leave type name in text-sm font-semibold text-slate-600, rendered as a flex row with gap-1.5 — e.g. 'Casual Leave', 'Earned Leave', 'Sick Leave', 'Comp Off', 'Unpaid Leave'; when the card is locked a 🔒 emoji (text-xs, tooltip 'Locked during probation') follows the name. Line 2 (the metric): the balance to exactly 2 decimal places in text-3xl font-bold text-slate-800, mt-2, immediately followed by the unit ' days' in text-base font-medium text-slate-400 — e.g. '7.50 days'. Line 3: a progress bar, mt-3, h-2, rounded-full, track bg-slate-100, fill bg-brand-600 rounded-full; fill width percent = min(100, round(balance / accrued × 100)), and is 0% whenever accrued is zero. Line 4: text-xs text-slate-500, mt-2, exactly 'accrued 9.00 · used 1.5 · +1.5/month' (accrued shown to 2 dp, used shown raw, then the monthly accrual rate with a leading +). LOCKED VARIANT (employee on probation and the type is not UL): the whole card gets bg-slate-50/65, border-slate-200, opacity-60, select-none; the big number turns text-slate-400 with a line-through; the progress bar is replaced by the text 'Locked during probation' in mt-3.5 text-[11px] font-semibold text-amber-600; and line 4 reads just 'Balance inactive'.

widgets.label: Balance summary table
widgets.detail: Full-width table, divide-y slate-200, header row bg-slate-50. Column headers in this exact order: 'Leave Type', 'Monthly Accrual', 'Accrued (total)', 'Used', 'Balance'. Header cells are px-4 py-3, text-left, text-xs, font-semibold, text-slate-500, UPPERCASE, tracking-wider. Body rows divide-y slate-100, hover:bg-slate-50, cells px-4 py-3 text-sm. Cell contents: 'Leave Type' = font-medium name followed by the code in parentheses in text-slate-400, e.g. 'Earned Leave (EL)', plus an amber pill Badge reading 'Locked' when the row is locked. 'Monthly Accrual' = the rate followed by the literal words ' days/month', e.g. '1.5 days/month'. 'Accrued (total)' = 2 decimal places. 'Used' = raw number. 'Balance' = 2 decimal places in font-semibold text-brand-700, or text-slate-400 with a line-through when locked. Locked rows get opacity-50, select-none and a faint bg-slate-50/20.

widgets.label: Ledger card heading block
widgets.detail: Inside the final card, px-4 pt-4 pb-1: h3 'How your balance was calculated' in font-bold text-slate-800, then a text-xs text-slate-500 line 'Every credit and deduction, most recent first.'

widgets.label: Balance ledger table
widgets.detail: Full-width table, mt-2, divide-y slate-200, header bg-slate-50. Column headers in this exact order: 'When', 'Type', 'Change', 'What', 'Details'. Cell contents: 'When' = timestamp formatted DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS, text-xs, whitespace-nowrap. 'Type' = the leave type CODE only (CL, EL, SL, CO, UL). 'Change' = the signed delta in font-semibold, prefixed with '+' when positive, coloured text-emerald-700 when >= 0 and text-red-600 when negative, e.g. '+1.5' or '-2'. 'What' = a pill Badge whose text and colour come from a fixed map: accrual → 'Monthly accrual' (blue, bg-blue-100/text-blue-700); adjustment → 'HR adjustment' (purple, bg-purple-100/text-purple-700); leave_taken → 'Leave taken' (red, bg-red-100/text-red-700); leave_cancelled → 'Leave cancelled' (green, bg-emerald-100/text-emerald-700). 'Details' = the free-text note, text-xs, capped at max-w-[320px]. The server returns at most 15 ledger rows, newest first.

widgets.label: Ledger empty row
widgets.detail: When there are no ledger entries, a single row spanning all 5 columns, centered, text-slate-500, py-8, reading exactly: 'No balance activity yet — HR grants leave via monthly accrual or manual credits.'

actions: 'Apply Leave' button in the header — navigates to /leave/apply.
Horizontal scroll on both tables when the viewport is narrower than the table.
states: Loading: the entire page body is replaced by a centred spinner — an 8×8 element, animate-spin, rounded-full, 4px border in slate-200 with a brand-600 top border, inside a flex-justify-center wrapper with py-16. No header is shown while loading.

Error: the entire page is replaced by a single red Alert (bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200) containing the API error string, e.g. 'No employee profile linked to this account'. The header, cards and tables are not rendered at all.
On probation: blue info alert appears; every non-UL stat card and table row renders in the greyed-out 'Locked' variant with strikethrough balances; the Unpaid Leave row/card stays normal.
Zero accrued: the progress bar renders at 0% width.
Empty ledger: the 5-column empty message row.
Loaded normally: no alerts, four-to-five stat cards, both tables populated.
mockData: Employee: Ananya Deshpande (EMP014). Stat cards / summary table rows: Casual Leave (CL) — monthly accrual 1 days/month, accrued 9.00, used 3, balance 6.00; Earned Leave (EL) — 1.5 days/month, accrued 13.50, used 6, balance 7.50; Sick Leave (SL) — 0.75 days/month, accrued 6.75, used 2, balance 4.75; Comp Off (CO) — 0 days/month, accrued 2.00, used 0, balance 2.00; Unpaid Leave (UL) — 0 days/month, accrued 0.00, used 4, balance 0.00. Ledger rows, newest first: '01/09/2026 00:05:12 | EL | +1.5 | Monthly accrual | Monthly accrual EL: 1 month(s) x 1.5 (up to 2026-09)'; '01/09/2026 00:05:12 | CL | +1 | Monthly accrual | Monthly accrual CL: 1 month(s) x 1 (up to 2026-09)'; '01/09/2026 00:05:11 | SL | +0.75 | Monthly accrual | Monthly accrual SL: 1 month(s) x 0.75 (up to 2026-09)'; '18/08/2026 11:42:09 | CL | -2 | Leave taken | Leave #218 approved (2026-08-20 to 2026-08-21)'; '12/08/2026 16:20:44 | CO | +2 | HR adjustment | Comp-off credited for Independence Day release support'; '05/08/2026 09:58:33 | EL | -3 | Leave taken | Leave #204 approved (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-12)'; '29/07/2026 14:07:19 | EL | +3 | Leave cancelled | Approved leave #191 cancelled (2026-07-30 to 2026-08-01)'; '01/08/2026 00:05:10 | EL | +1.5 | Monthly accrual | Monthly accrual EL: 1 month(s) x 1.5 (up to 2026-08)'. Probation-variant employee for the locked screenshot: Nikhil Bhatt (EMP031), 'probation until 31/01/2027'. Note: this screen shows no currency — balances are in days only.

title: Leave History
purpose: Lists every leave application the logged-in employee has ever filed with its approval outcome, and lets them edit or cancel the ones still pending.
layout: Single column. (1) PageHeader, mb-6: h1 'Leave History' (text-2xl bold slate-800), subtitle 'All leave applications and their status — pending ones can be edited or cancelled' (text-sm slate-500). No header action buttons. (2) Conditional red error alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (3) Conditional green success alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (4) A single .card with overflow-x-auto wrapping one wide 10-column table (min-w-full, divide-y slate-200, header row bg-slate-50, body rows divide-y slate-100 with hover:bg-slate-50). (5) An edit Modal rendered on top when a row's Edit is clicked.

widgets.label: Leave applications table
widgets.detail: Ten columns, header cells px-4 py-3 text-left text-xs font-semibold text-slate-500 UPPERCASE tracking-wider, in this exact order: 'Applied', 'Type', 'Dates', 'Days', 'Document', 'Status', 'Decided By', 'Decision Date', 'Rejection Reason', and a tenth header that is deliberately EMPTY (it sits above the row-action buttons). Body cells are px-4 py-3 text-sm. Column contents: (1) Applied = date as DD/MM/YYYY, whitespace-nowrap. (2) Type = the leave type name, followed when the leave is unpaid by an amber pill Badge reading 'Unpaid' (ml-1.5, bg-amber-100/text-amber-700). (3) Dates = 'DD/MM/YYYY → DD/MM/YYYY' with a literal right-arrow between them, whitespace-nowrap. (4) Days = the working-day count, may be a decimal. (5) Document = when an attachment exists, an inline button showing a lucide Paperclip at 13px followed by the word 'View', styled text-brand-600 text-sm font-medium with hover:underline; when there is no attachment the cell shows an em dash '—'. (6) Status = a pill Badge; the label is re-mapped so 'Pending' displays as 'Awaiting Approval' (amber), while 'Approved' shows as 'Approved' (green/emerald), 'Rejected' as 'Rejected' (red) and 'Cancelled' as 'Cancelled' (slate grey). (7) Decided By = the approver's name and role in the format 'Priya Sharma (HR)', or '—'. (8) Decision Date = DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS, whitespace-nowrap, or '—'. (9) Rejection Reason = free text capped at max-w-[220px], or '—'. (10) Row actions = rendered ONLY when the status is Pending: a right-aligned flex row, gap-2, containing an 'Edit' button (lucide Pencil at 13px plus the word 'Edit', text-brand-600 text-sm font-medium, hover:underline) and a 'Cancel' button (text-red-600 text-sm font-medium, hover:underline). Non-pending rows leave this cell blank. Rows are sorted newest-applied first.

widgets.label: Empty state row
widgets.detail: When the employee has filed nothing, a single row spanning all 10 columns, centered, text-slate-500, py-10, reading exactly: 'No leave applications yet.'

widgets.label: Error alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200 alert, mb-4, showing the API error verbatim, e.g. 'Only pending applications can be edited (this one is Approved)', 'You can only edit your own applications', 'Already Cancelled', 'Failed to fetch document'.

widgets.label: Success alert (conditional, auto-dismiss)
widgets.detail: bg-emerald-50 / text-emerald-700 / border-emerald-200 alert, mb-4, auto-clears after 4 seconds. Messages seen here: 'Leave application cancelled' (after a row Cancel) and 'Leave application updated (3 working day(s)) — the approvers have been notified.' (after a modal save).

widgets.label: Edit Leave Application modal
widgets.detail: Opens centred over a bg-slate-900/50 backdrop (clicking the backdrop closes it). Panel is a .card, w-full, max-w-lg, max-h-[90vh] with vertical scroll, p-6, z-50. Header row: title in text-lg font-bold text-slate-800 reading 'Edit Leave Application #218' (the literal application id), and a '×' close button on the right in text-2xl text-slate-400 hover:text-slate-600. Body is a form with space-y-4: FIELD 1 'LEAVE TYPE' — a .input <select>, required, listing every leave type by name with NO placeholder option (Casual Leave, Earned Leave, Sick Leave, Comp Off, Unpaid Leave), pre-selected to the application's current type. FIELD 2 — a 2-column grid, gap-4: 'FROM DATE' and 'TO DATE', both NATIVE <input type="date"> controls with class .input (note: this modal uses the browser's native date picker, NOT the custom DatePicker used on the Apply screen), both required, To Date carrying min = the From Date. FIELD 3 'REASON' — a .input <textarea>, rows=3, required, pre-filled with the existing reason. FIELD 4 'REPLACE DOCUMENT (OPTIONAL)' — a NATIVE <input type="file"> styled with class .input, accept='.pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.doc,.docx', followed by a text-xs text-slate-400 note, mt-1: 'Leave empty to keep the current document. The approvers are re-notified after saving.' FOOTER — a right-aligned flex row, gap-2: a .btn-secondary button labelled 'Cancel' (white, border-slate-300, text-slate-700) and a .btn-primary submit labelled 'Save Changes', which becomes 'Saving…' and disabled while the save is in flight.

widgets.label: Cancel confirmation (native browser confirm)
widgets.detail: Clicking a row's 'Cancel' fires the browser's own confirm() dialog with the exact text 'Cancel this leave application?'. There is no custom-styled confirmation modal. Dismissing it aborts; confirming sends the delete.

actions: 'View' in the Document column — fetches the protected attachment as a blob and opens it in a new browser tab; a failure surfaces in the red error alert instead.
'Edit' on a Pending row — opens the Edit Leave Application modal pre-filled with that row's type, dates and reason.

'Cancel' on a Pending row — DESTRUCTIVE. Shows the native confirm 'Cancel this leave application?'; on confirm sends DELETE /api/leaves/:id, which moves the application to status 'Cancelled', shows the green 'Leave application cancelled' alert and reloads the table. Only Pending (and, for approvers, Approved) applications can be cancelled; already-Rejected or already-Cancelled ones are refused by the server.

'Save Changes' in the modal — sends PUT /api/leaves/:id as multipart, recalculates the working-day count, closes the modal, reloads the table and shows 'Leave application updated (3 working day(s)) — the approvers have been notified.'
'Cancel' button or the '×' in the modal, or a click on the dark backdrop — closes the modal discarding edits.
Horizontal scroll of the table on narrow viewports.
states: Loading: the whole page body is replaced by the centred spinner (8×8, animate-spin, 4px slate-200 border with brand-600 top, py-16 wrapper).
Hard error before any data arrives: the page renders only a red Alert with the error text — no header, no table.
Soft error after data has loaded: the table stays on screen and the red Alert appears above it.
Success: green alert above the table for 4 seconds, then it disappears on its own.
Empty: the single 'No leave applications yet.' row across all 10 columns.
Per-row conditional: the action column renders Edit/Cancel only for status 'Pending'; Approved, Rejected and Cancelled rows show an empty action cell.
Per-row conditional: the amber 'Unpaid' badge appears next to the type only for unpaid applications (unpaid leave type, or any leave taken while on probation).
Per-row conditional: the Document cell shows the 'View' button only when a file was attached, otherwise an em dash.
Saving: the modal's primary button is disabled and reads 'Saving…'.
No permission gate — every authenticated employee sees their own history only.

title: Leave Approvals
purpose: The approval inbox for HR, the Director, or anyone granted the leaves.approve permission — each pending leave request is shown as a card that can be approved outright or rejected with a written reason.
layout: Single column. (1) PageHeader, mb-6: h1 'Leave Approvals' (text-2xl bold slate-800), subtitle 'One approval from you fully approves the request (HR / Director)' (text-sm slate-500). No header action buttons. (2) Conditional red error alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (3) Conditional green success alert in a mb-4 wrapper. (4) The body is EITHER the empty-inbox card OR a responsive card grid — 1 column on mobile, 2 columns at lg, gap-4 — with one request card per pending application, ordered oldest-applied first. (5) A reject Modal rendered on top when Reject is clicked. Note this page is card-based, NOT a table.

widgets.label: Pending request card (repeated in a 2-up grid)
widgets.detail: A .card with p-5. TOP ROW: flex, items-start, justify-between, gap-3. Left side — line 1: the employee's full name in font-semibold text-slate-800 followed by their employee code in parentheses in text-slate-400 font-normal, e.g. 'Sneha Iyer (EMP004)'; line 2 (mt-0.5, text-sm text-slate-600): the leave type, the date range and the day count joined by middot separators, e.g. 'Casual Leave · 03/08/2026 → 04/08/2026 · 2 days' where the '2 days' fragment is font-medium and 'day' is singular when the count is 1. Right side — a vertical flex column, items-end, gap-1, of pill badges: always a status Badge whose text is the literal string 'Awaiting Approval' (amber, since the underlying status is always Pending here), and beneath it, only for unpaid requests, a second amber Badge reading 'Unpaid (probation)'. REASON BLOCK (mt-3): a text-sm text-slate-600 paragraph on a bg-slate-50 panel, rounded-lg, p-3, border border-slate-100, reading 'Reason: <the employee's text>' with the word 'Reason:' in font-medium text-slate-500. ATTACHMENT LINK (conditional, mt-2): a lucide Paperclip at 14px followed by the text 'View attached document', styled text-sm text-brand-600 font-medium with hover:underline. APPLIED LINE (mt-2): text-xs text-slate-400 reading 'Applied 01/08/2026'. BUTTON ROW (mt-4): flex, gap-2.5, both buttons flex-1 and py-2 so they split the card width evenly — see the button-row widget.

widgets.label: Approve / Reject buttons on each card
widgets.detail: Two equal-width buttons. LEFT: a lucide Check icon at 16px plus the word 'Approve', styled bg-emerald-50 with hover:bg-emerald-100, text-emerald-700, border border-emerald-200, rounded-lg, py-2, flex-1. RIGHT: a lucide X icon at 16px plus the word 'Reject', styled bg-red-50 with hover:bg-red-100, text-red-700, border border-red-200, rounded-lg, py-2, flex-1. Approve fires immediately with no confirmation step; Reject opens the modal.

widgets.label: Empty inbox state
widgets.detail: Replaces the whole grid. A .card with p-12, laid out as a centred vertical flex column with centred text: a lucide Inbox icon at 40px in text-slate-300 with mb-3; then 'Nothing waiting for approval' in font-semibold text-slate-700; then, mt-1, 'New leave applications will appear here (and in your email).' in text-sm text-slate-500.

widgets.label: Reject Leave Application modal
widgets.detail: Centred over a bg-slate-900/50 backdrop (click to close). Panel is a .card, w-full, max-w-lg, max-h-[90vh] scrollable, p-6. Header: title 'Reject Leave Application' in text-lg font-bold text-slate-800, plus a '×' close button in text-2xl text-slate-400 hover:text-slate-600. Body form, space-y-4: one field, label 'REJECTION REASON', a .input <textarea> with rows=3, required, placeholder 'Why is this request being rejected?'. Footer: right-aligned flex row, gap-2 — a .btn-secondary button labelled 'Cancel', and the submit button labelled 'Reject Application' styled bg-red-50 with hover:bg-red-100, text-red-700, border border-red-200, rounded-lg, py-2 px-4.

widgets.label: Error alert (conditional)
widgets.detail: bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-200 alert, mb-4. Real messages: 'Forbidden' / a 403 permission error for users without leaves.approve, 'Leave application not found', 'Already Approved', 'Failed to fetch document'.

widgets.label: Success alert (conditional, auto-dismiss)
widgets.detail: bg-emerald-50 / text-emerald-700 / border-emerald-200 alert, mb-4, clears itself after 4 seconds. Exact messages: 'Leave approved — the employee and their manager have been emailed.' after an approval, and 'Leave application rejected' after a rejection.

actions: 'Approve' on a card — POSTs immediately with NO confirmation dialog. Deducts the days from the employee's balance (unless the leave is unpaid), writes a ledger entry, marks the attendance days as 'Leave', emails the employee and their reporting manager, removes the card from the inbox and shows the green 'Leave approved — the employee and their manager have been emailed.' alert.
'Reject' on a card — opens the Reject Leave Application modal for that request.

'Reject Application' in the modal — submits the typed reason, marks the request Rejected (the reason becomes the 'Rejection Reason' the employee sees in their history), closes the modal, removes the card and shows 'Leave application rejected'.
'Cancel' button or '×' in the modal, or a backdrop click — closes the modal without rejecting.
'View attached document' — fetches the protected file as a blob and opens it in a new tab; a failure surfaces in the red error alert.
states: Loading: the whole body is replaced by the centred spinner (8×8, animate-spin, 4px slate-200 border with brand-600 top, py-16 wrapper). Shown while there are neither rows nor an error yet.
Empty: the Inbox-icon card, 'Nothing waiting for approval'.
Populated: the 2-up card grid, oldest request first.
Error: the red alert renders above whatever body state applies; if the fetch failed outright the grid never appears.
Success: green alert for 4 seconds, and the list silently refetches so the acted-on card disappears.
Per-card conditional: the amber 'Unpaid (probation)' badge only on unpaid requests; the 'View attached document' link only when a file was attached.

Permission-denied: the route is gated by the leaves.approve permission — the 'Approvals' item is not even rendered in the sidebar for users without it, and a direct visit gets a 403 from the API which lands in the red error alert with an empty body.
Self-request filtering: your own pending request is hidden from your inbox — except for a company owner/director, who has nobody above them and therefore still sees their own request listed.

title: Payroll Management
purpose: Lets an HR/payroll user pick a payroll cycle, see every active employee's gross pay against that cycle's LOP/EL/SL/WFH day counts, export the full salary sheet as CSV, and generate an individual salary slip PDF after tweaking the amounts.
layout:
THIS IS THE DEFAULT TAB of the single Next.js route /admin/payroll. The page has client-side tab state (useState 'Run Payroll') — there is NO second URL; the Salary Structures screen documented separately is the same route with the other tab selected.

APP SHELL (components/AppShell.jsx, wraps every /admin/* page). Page background slate-100 (#f1f5f9), font stack ui-sans-serif / system-ui / Segoe UI / Roboto. Fixed left sidebar 256px (w-64), full height, bg-slate-900, visible at lg and up; below lg it is hidden and opens as an overlay drawer (absolute inset-y-0 left-0 w-64 over a slate-900/60 scrim) from a hamburger in the top bar. Main column is offset by lg:pl-64 and contains a sticky white top bar (border-b slate-200, px-4 lg:px-8, py-3) then <main class='p-4 lg:p-8'>.

MAIN CONTENT, top to bottom:
1. PageHeader — flex row, wraps, justify-between, mb-6. h1 'Payroll Management' at text-2xl font-bold slate-800; subtitle beneath it at text-sm slate-500 mt-0.5. No right-hand action slot is used on this page.
2. Alert slot — success then error banner, full width, rounded-lg with 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm. NOTE: the page passes className='mb-4' but the Alert component does not accept or apply className, so the banners render flush against the next block with no bottom gap. Reproduce that flush spacing.
3. Control row — flex flex-col on mobile, sm:flex-row sm:items-center justify-between, gap-4, mb-6. Left: a two-button tab strip in a container with border-b border-slate-200, flex gap-4, overflow-x-auto, w-full sm:w-auto flex-1. Right: a search field, w-full sm:w-72, relative, with a magnifier SVG absolutely positioned left-3 top-3 (w-4 h-4, slate-400) and the input given pl-9.
4. Filter/period card — .card (bg-white rounded-xl border border-slate-200 shadow-sm), p-4, flex gap-4 items-end, single row that does NOT wrap. Order: Month select, Year number input, the 'Paying for' period readout, then a spacer (ml-auto) pushing the Export Excel button to the far right.
5. Table card — .card with overflow-x-auto, no padding; a full-bleed 8-column table fills it edge to edge. thead bg-slate-50; tbody rows divided by divide-y divide-slate-100; row hover bg-slate-50. While the cycle is loading the whole table is replaced by a centred spinner inside this same card.
6. Modal overlay (only when a row's action is clicked) — fixed inset-0 z-50, flex centred, p-4; a slate-900/50 backdrop; panel is .card w-full max-w-lg (512px), max-h-[90vh], overflow-y-auto, p-6, with a header row (bold 18px slate-800 title on the left, a slate-400 '×' at text-2xl on the right, mb-4).

widgets.label: Sidebar navigation (app shell)
widgets.detail: Dark slate-900 column, 256px. Top: product logo at 30px in its light variant, on a border-b border-slate-800 block with px-5 py-5. Below it a company block (px-5 py-2.5, border-b slate-800): an 11px uppercase tracking-wide slate-500 label 'Company' over the company name at text-sm font-semibold slate-200. Then a scrolling nav (px-3 py-4, space-y-1) whose items for an HR user are, in order: collapsible group 'Home' (children: Home, Dashboard); collapsible group 'Attendance & Leave' (children: Attendance, Leave Balance, Apply Leave, Leave History, Approvals); collapsible group 'Documents' (children: Salary Slips, Offer Letter, Company Policies); a flat link 'Payroll' -> /admin/payroll with a banknote icon — THIS IS THE ACTIVE ITEM on this screen; then a section header 'MANAGEMENT' (11px, font-semibold, uppercase, tracking-wider, slate-500, px-3 pb-1) over flat links Overview, Employees, Attendance, Leave Management, Leave Balances, Documents, Reports, Analytics, Settings, Email Log; then a flat link 'Change Password'. Flat links: flex, gap-3, rounded-lg, px-3 py-2.5, text-sm font-medium, 18px lucide icon. Active = bg-brand-600 (#1d4ed8) with white text; inactive = slate-300 text, hover bg-slate-800 + white. Group headers are buttons with the same padding plus a right-aligned 16px chevron that rotates 180deg when open; expanded children sit in a ml-4 mt-1 block with a border-l border-slate-700 and pl-3, each child px-3 py-2 text-sm with a 15px icon, slate-400, active child bg-brand-600 white font-medium. Footer (border-t slate-800, p-3): a full-width 'Logout' button, slate-300, 18px logout icon, hover bg-red-600/90 with white text.

widgets.label: Top bar (app shell)
widgets.detail: Sticky, white, border-b slate-200, flex justify-between, px-4 lg:px-8 py-3. Left: a 22px hamburger shown only below lg, then a text-sm slate-500 line reading 'FOne HR — {company name}' (hidden below sm). Right (flex, gap-5): a notification bell button (20px lucide Bell in a rounded-full p-1.5 hover:bg-slate-100 slate-500 button) carrying a red unread badge — a 16px min-width rounded-full bg-red-500 pill with white 9px bold text and a 2px white ring, positioned -top-1 -right-1; then the identity block (flex gap-3): right-aligned text with the user's full name at text-sm font-semibold slate-800 over '{ROLE} · {EMP_CODE}' at text-xs slate-500, followed by a 36px rounded-full bg-brand-600 avatar with white text-sm font-bold initials (first letter of each of the first two name words).

widgets.label: Payroll section tabs
widgets.detail: Exactly two tabs, in this order: 'Run Payroll' (active/default) and 'Salary Structures'. Each is a button with pb-3 px-1, text-sm font-medium, whitespace-nowrap, border-b-2. Active: border-brand-600 (#1d4ed8) with text-brand-700 (#1e40af). Inactive: border-transparent, text-slate-500, hover text-slate-700 and hover border-slate-300. They sit on a shared border-b border-slate-200 rail with gap-4 between them. Switching tabs changes nothing in the URL and does not refetch the employee or structure lists.

widgets.label: Employee search box
widgets.detail: A single text input, placeholder 'Search by name or ID...', styled with the .input class (w-full, rounded-lg, 1px slate-300 border, px-3 py-2, text-sm, white, focus ring-2 brand-500) plus pl-9 to clear a 16px slate-400 magnifier icon pinned at left-3 top-3. Width w-full below sm, 288px (w-72) at sm and up. It is rendered ONCE in the shared header and filters BOTH tabs' tables from the same structures array. Matching is case-insensitive substring against three fields checked independently — first_name, last_name, emp_code — so 'iy' matches Sneha Iyer and 'emp00' matches EMP001 through EMP009, but the combined string 'sneha iyer' matches nothing.

widgets.label: Month selector
widgets.detail: Label 'Month' rendered with the .label class (block, text-xs, font-semibold, slate-600, UPPERCASE, tracking-wide, mb-1 — so it visually reads 'MONTH'). Control is a <select class='input'> with exactly twelve options in calendar order: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December, whose values are 1-12. Defaults to the current month (September for a 2026-09-21 render). Changing it refetches the cycle's LOP counts and period from /payroll/lop/{year}/{month}. Not required, cannot be blank.

widgets.label: Year input
widgets.detail: Label 'Year' via .label (renders as 'YEAR'). Control is <input type='number' class='input'> with no min, max or step attributes — a free spinner. Defaults to the current year (2026). Every keystroke that parses to a number refetches the cycle. Not required.

widgets.label: 'Paying for' period readout
widgets.detail: Conditional — rendered only once the /payroll/lop response has arrived with a period object; before that the whole block is absent (not a placeholder, not a skeleton). Two stacked lines, self-end with pb-2: line one 'Paying for' at text-xs slate-400 leading-tight; line two at text-sm font-medium slate-600 leading-tight reading '{label} · {days} days'. The label is the payroll CYCLE, not the calendar month — the company runs a 25th-to-24th cycle, so choosing September 2026 shows '25 Aug – 24 Sep 2026 · 31 days' (en dash, spaces either side, middle-dot separator). A cycle that crosses the year boundary shows the start year too: January 2026 is '25 Dec 2025 – 24 Jan 2026 · 31 days'. The days number is the real length of the window and is the divisor used for one day's pay.

widgets.label: Export Excel button
widgets.detail: Single .btn-secondary (white, 1px slate-300 border, slate-700 text, rounded-lg, px-4 py-2, text-sm font-medium, hover bg-slate-50), containing a 16px lucide Download icon with mr-1 then the text 'Export Excel'. Pushed to the far right of the filter card by an ml-auto wrapper. Despite the label it downloads a CSV, named payroll-2026-09.csv (year, then zero-padded month).

widgets.label: Run Payroll table
widgets.detail: Eight columns, in exactly this rendered order: 'Employee' | 'Monthly Salary (Gross)' | 'LOP Days' | 'EL' | 'SL' | 'WFH' | 'Est. LOP Ded (₹)' | 'Actions'. Header cells use .th — px-4 py-3, text-left, text-xs, font-semibold, slate-500, UPPERCASE, tracking-wider — on a bg-slate-50 thead, so they display as 'EMPLOYEE', 'MONTHLY SALARY (GROSS)', 'LOP DAYS', 'EL', 'SL', 'WFH', 'EST. LOP DED (₹)', 'ACTIONS'. Body cells use .td — px-4 py-3, text-sm. Cell rules: Employee is '{emp_code} - {first_name} {last_name}' (a plain hyphen with a space each side) at font-medium; Monthly Salary is basic+hra+special_allowance+conveyance printed as a bare JavaScript number with NO rupee sign, NO thousands separators and NO decimals (e.g. 53000, 191600); LOP Days prints a plain '0' when zero and the number in text-rose-600 font-bold when above zero; EL and SL print '0' when zero and text-amber-600 font-bold when above zero; WFH prints '0' when zero and text-blue-600 font-bold when above zero; Est. LOP Ded is always text-rose-600 font-medium and equals round((gross / period.days) * lopDays * 100) / 100, again printed as a raw number so trailing zeros are dropped (5612.9, not 5,612.90) and an em dash '—' is shown instead if the period has not loaded; Actions holds one button. Rows are ordered by first name then last name (server-side). No row striping, no checkboxes, no pagination, no sortable headers, no totals/footer row, no status pills anywhere on this page.

widgets.label: Row action: Edit & Generate Slip
widgets.detail: One per table row, in the Actions cell. A .btn-primary (bg-brand-600 #1d4ed8, white text, rounded-lg, hover bg-brand-700) with padding and size overridden to !py-1 and !text-xs so it is a compact pill, containing a 14px lucide FileText icon then the text 'Edit & Generate Slip' (the ampersand is rendered as a literal &).

widgets.label: Modal: Edit & Generate Slip
widgets.detail:
Title 'Edit & Generate Slip'. Panel max-w-lg (512px), max-h-[90vh], overflow-y-auto, p-6, over a slate-900/50 backdrop; header row with the title at text-lg font-bold slate-800 and a slate-400 '×' at text-2xl. Body is a <form class='space-y-4'> whose first child is a grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 containing three labelled sections and eleven fields. Every field label uses .label so all labels render UPPERCASE. NO field in this modal is marked required.
SECTION 1 heading, spanning both columns with border-b pb-2: 'Salary Components'. Fields: 'Basic' — number, step 0.01, blanked to an empty box when the value is 0; 'HRA' — number, step 0.01, blanked when 0; 'Special Allowance' — number, step 0.01, blanked when 0; 'Conveyance' — number, step 0.01, shows a literal 0 rather than blanking (defaults to 1600).
SECTION 2 heading, col-span-2, border-b pb-2 mt-2: 'Deductions & Attendance'. Fields: 'PF Deduction' — number, step 0.01; 'Tax (TDS)' — number, step 0.01; 'LOP Days' — number, step 0.5 (half days are real); 'Est. LOP Deduction' — type TEXT, disabled, bg-slate-50, read-only computed mirror of the table's estimate.
SECTION 3 heading, col-span-2, border-b pb-2 mt-2: 'Other Attendance (For Record)'. Fields: 'EL Days' — number, step 0.5, blanked when 0; 'SL Days' — number, step 0.5, blanked when 0; 'WFH Days' — number, step 0.5, blanked when 0. These three sit in a two-column grid, so the last grid cell of this section is empty — leave the gap.
NET PAY STRIP, below the grid, mt-4: bg-slate-50, p-3, rounded, 1px border, flex justify-between items-center. Left 'Net Pay (Calculated):' at font-bold slate-700. Right 'Rs. {amount}' — the literal prefix 'Rs. ' (not ₹) followed by a two-decimal number, at font-bold text-brand-700 text-lg. Net = gross − PF − Tax − LOP deduction. ESIC is deliberately NOT subtracted here even though it is sent to the server, so the preview can read higher than the eventual slip.
FOOTER: flex justify-end gap-2 pt-2 — 'Cancel' (.btn-secondary) then 'Generate Slip' (.btn-primary with a 16px FileText icon).

widgets.label: Success alert banner
widgets.detail: Emerald toast rendered above the tab strip: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-emerald-50, text-emerald-700, border-emerald-200. Auto-clears after 4 seconds. On this tab it says 'Generated slip for {first} {last}'.

widgets.label: Error alert banner
widgets.detail: Red toast in the same slot: rounded-lg, 1px border, px-4 py-3, text-sm, bg-red-50, text-red-700, border-red-200. Auto-clears after 5 seconds. Text is whatever the API returned ('Request failed', 'Forbidden', 'Failed to fetch document'), or the client-side message 'The payroll period has not loaded yet — reload before generating a slip.'

actions: Click the 'Run Payroll' tab — already active here; switches the body view, does not touch the URL or refetch anything.
Click the 'Salary Structures' tab — swaps the body to the nine-column structures table; the search box and its current query stay put and keep applying.

Type in 'Search by name or ID...' — live-filters the table on every keystroke by first name, last name or employee code (case-insensitive substring, each field checked separately). Filtering is purely client-side; no request is made.
Change the Month select — refetches /payroll/lop/{year}/{month}, replacing the LOP/EL/SL/WFH columns, the 'Paying for' readout and every Est. LOP Ded value. Shows the in-card spinner while it runs.
Change the Year input — same refetch as Month, fired on every parsed keystroke.

Click 'Export Excel' — GETs /payroll/export/{year}/{month} with the auth token, turns the response into a blob and triggers a browser download named payroll-2026-09.csv. The CSV is a wide attendance-plus-salary sheet: Sl. No, Name, Designation, DOJ, then one column per day of the cycle (weekday name over the date), then Total No. Of days, Present Days, Absent Days, Days to be processed for Salary, Annual Salary, Monthly Salary, Per Day, Salary Amount to be processed, Remarks, Bank name, Account no, IFSC. SENSITIVE: it exports every active employee's salary and bank account details in one file, and the server writes a PAYROLL_EXPORTED audit entry. A failure surfaces in the red alert banner.
Click a row's 'Edit & Generate Slip' — opens the slip modal prefilled from that employee's saved structure plus that cycle's LOP, EL, SL and WFH day counts. Read-only until something is submitted.
Close the slip modal via the '×', the 'Cancel' button, or a click on the dark backdrop — discards every edit; nothing is saved and no request is sent.

Edit any amount or day count inside the modal — recomputes the Est. LOP Deduction box and the Net Pay strip live. Changes here apply only to the slip being generated; they do NOT write back to the saved salary structure.

Click 'Generate Slip' (submit) — POSTs to /documents/salary-slips with employee_id, month, year, basic, hra, special_allowance, conveyance, pf_deduction, esic_deduction, tax_deduction, lop_deduction, pan_no, bank_name, bank_account_no and bank_ifsc, creating a salary-slip PDF the employee will see under Documents > Salary Slips. On success the modal closes and the green toast reads 'Generated slip for Sneha Iyer'. CONSEQUENTIAL and one-way from this screen: the table does not change, no 'generated' tick or badge appears anywhere, the row can be submitted again, and deleting a slip is only possible from /admin/documents.
Click any sidebar link or the Logout button — standard app-shell navigation; Logout clears the stored session and returns to /login.
states: Initial load — the ENTIRE page body (header, tabs, search, everything) is replaced by a single centred spinner: a 32px circle, 4px border in slate-200 with a brand-600 top edge, spinning, inside a flex justify-center py-16 wrapper. It clears once both /employees and /payroll/structures resolve.

Zero active employees — the guard is `!employees.length || !structures`, so a company with no active staff sits on that full-page spinner forever. There is no empty state, no 'no employees yet' message and no call to action. Worth mocking as a distinct 'permanent loading' frame.

Cycle loading — once the page itself has rendered, changing month or year sets a local loading flag: the filter card stays fully visible and interactive while the table card's contents are swapped for the same centred spinner. The eight column headers disappear with it.

Search with no matches — the table renders the thead and an empty tbody. There is no 'No results' row, no illustration and no 'clear search' affordance: just column headers over blank space inside the card.

Period not yet loaded — the whole 'Paying for' block is absent from the filter card (the row simply gets shorter), and every Est. LOP Ded cell shows an em dash '—' instead of a number. If Generate Slip is submitted in this state the POST is skipped and the red banner shows 'The payroll period has not loaded yet — reload before generating a slip.'
Success — emerald banner above the tab strip for 4 seconds, then it vanishes and the layout shifts up.
Error — red banner in the same slot for 5 seconds. Any of the four requests on this screen (employees, structures, LOP, export) can populate it.

Alert spacing quirk — both banners are given className='mb-4' by the page, but the Alert component ignores className entirely, so they render flush against the control row with no bottom margin. Reproduce the flush spacing, not a gap.

Permission denied — the whole screen is gated on the documents.manage permission. A user without it never sees the Payroll link in the sidebar at all (the nav is built from permissions, so the item is omitted rather than disabled), and a direct visit renders the page chrome with a red API error banner and empty tables. A 401 clears the stored session and hard-redirects to /login.
Platform-admin view — the Payroll nav entry is only built for non-platform users, so a platform admin operating inside a company never gets this link in the sidebar.

Modals — both start closed. Only one can be open at a time. Opening one does not dim or freeze the page behind it beyond the 50% slate backdrop; the panel scrolls internally once it exceeds 90% of the viewport height.
After a slip is generated — nothing on the table changes. No badge, no row highlight, no count, no list of already-generated slips for the cycle. The only feedback is the 4-second toast.

Mobile / narrow — below sm the tab strip and the search box stack vertically and the search goes full width; the tab strip scrolls horizontally inside its rail. Below lg the sidebar collapses to a hamburger drawer and the top bar's company line is hidden. Both tables scroll horizontally inside their card. The filter card is a non-wrapping flex row, so Month, Year, the period readout and Export Excel get cramped and clip on narrow screens — that is the real behaviour.

LOP Deduction 5612.9 (greyed and disabled), EL Days blank, SL Days blank, WFH Days blank, and the strip reading 'Net Pay (Calculated):' / 'Rs. 48737.10'.
